《字林西报》，
1939年6月7日
14179

英国人在与日本人的冲突中受重伤

R. M. 廷克勒先生在伦钟纱厂罢工事件后被拘捕；日方指控其向军官开枪

据指控，当一队日本海军陆战队水兵护送一群曾发生斗殴的中国罢工工人和顶替者穿过位于浦东角的英资伦钟纱厂（Lun Chong mill）厂区时，该厂45岁的英国劳工人事官员 R. M. 廷克勒先生向一名日本海军陆战队军官用手枪开了一枪，并用武器威胁驻浦东的日本海军陆战队指挥官野路 Munessuke 中校（Lieut.-Commdr. Munesuke Noji，音译）。廷克勒先生虽被陆战队成员打成重伤，但昨天全天被拘留在浦东，直到深夜才被带至上海，随即被紧急送往广慈医院（General Hospital）进行急诊手术。在廷克勒先生接受手术期间，日本海军陆战队员守在手术室门外。手术由两名日本海军外科医生和两名德国外科医生共同实施。

据悉，廷克勒先生头皮受伤，腹部有三处刺伤，腿部有一处刺伤。在日本海军发言人昨晚发表的声明中，称廷克勒先生是被步枪枪托击中的，并未提及任何刺伤情节。

该发言人透露，目前尚未决定是将廷克勒先生移交给英国当局，还是由日本军事法庭审判。与此事相关，三浦 Y. 先生（Mr. Y. Miura，音译）于昨日下午5时前往英国领事馆，提出“非常强烈的抗议”，并保留向英国当局提出进一步要求的权利。

在记者招待会上，该发言人称：“今天上午（星期二），伦钟纱厂发生了一起新的事件。自5月24日起，日本海军陆战队应英国当局的要求，一直在保护该厂财产。5月25日，驻扎在厂内的英军部队撤离，5月27日，部分日本海军陆战队队员进入厂内，以便更好地保护财产。

“5月30日，在英国军队旅参谋长在场的情况下，日本海军当局与厂方经理就以下几点达成了谅解：日本海军陆战队同意不偏不倚地保护伦钟纱厂；一旦条件允许，陆战队即行撤离；如发生骚乱，日本当局将采取措施予以处理。

工人斗殴

“此外，还就发生骚乱时如何向日军发出通知达成了详细协议。5月31日，浦东海军陆战队总部与纱厂之间建立了电话联络，随后陆战队撤离。此外，日本海军陆战队在一个可以俯瞰厂区的位置设立了瞭望哨，并保持了足够的人员待命，以应对可能出现的任何紧急情况。这是一项格外善意的措施。

pages.en:
"At about 7.50 a.m. today (Tuesday) Chinese millhands not participating in the strike arrived at the pontoon from the International Settlement. About 30 strikers who, apparently had been lying in wait near by on another sampan, began attacking the workers with sticks as soon as they arrived.
"The Landing Party lookout upon seeing this, sent ten sailors with an officer in charge to the pontoon to put a stop to the fight which was going on between the strikers and strikebreakers, who were herded together and escorted by the Japanese sailors to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters.

"Carried Pistols"

"In doing so they had to pass through the Lun Chong property and as they were marching there they approached the offices of the mill. About ten Britons appeared from the offices of the mill and three of them carried pistols. About fifteen of those Chinese who had been herded together (later found to be strikers) ran away from the group and headed for the power plant of the mill.
"The officer then detailed six sailors to pursue these 15 men to prevent them from running away and doing damage to the power plant. The officer left found men in charge of the remainder and went himself in the direction of the power plant. At this time the British employees of the mill approached the sailors and asked that the men working at the mill be handed over. This was refused. The British employees then began wrestling with the sailors in an attempt to get their rifles away.
"One shot was fired at the sailors by one of these Britons (Tinkler) and he then ran in the direction of the power plant. On approaching the Japanese officer in charge of the party he seized the officer' right forearm with his left hand and then pressed the gun against the officer and told him to get out from the plant. By that time the strikers who had run away had been rounded up outside the power plant by the six sailors.

Alleged Actions

"The Japanese officer in charge of the small party then asked for reinforcements and at the same time the Battalion Commander, who was about to leave the Battalion Headquarters to go to the Naval Landing Party Headquarters in Shanghai, received a request from the mill that help was needed as trouble had broken out.
"The Battalion Commander then sent re-inforcements which arrived at the mill at 8.10, arriving himself at 8.15. When he arrived on the scene the Briton with the gun pointed it at the Battalion Commander three times in succession, at the same time knocking him and threatening to kill him. In addition he went running around pointing his gun at officers and sailors.

Hit by Sailor

"In view of the danger involved of letting a man like that run around with a loaded gun a sailor seized the man and disarmed him. As shown by the preceding events the Landing Party showed admirable patience but this Englishman, who had been disarmed, then jumped upon the sailor and wanted to fight him.
"In view of this assault by this Briton another sailor seized his rifle and with the butt of the weapon hit him. The man was taken later to Battalion Headquarters. Previous to this there had been an understanding between the manager of the plant and the Commander of the Japanese Naval Landing Party in Pootung that no arms should be used on the plant without an understanding being reached with the Commander. This was only natural, as the Landing Party had agreed to protect the property.
pages.zh:
“今天上午（星期二）约7时50分，未参与罢工的中国工人从公共租界抵达浮码头。大约30名罢工者显然一直在附近的一艘舢板上埋伏，当工人们一到达，他们便开始用棍棒攻击这些工人。

“陆战队瞭望哨看到这一情况后，派出一名军官带领十名水兵前往浮码头，制止罢工者与顶替者之间的斗殴。这些人被聚集在一起，由日本水兵护送至日本海军陆战队总部。

‘携带手枪’

“在此过程中，他们必须穿过伦钟纱厂的厂区。当他们行进至此时，接近了厂方的办公楼。约有十名英国人从办公楼出现，其中三人携带手枪。约十五名被聚集在一起的中国人（后查明为罢工者）从人群中跑出，朝电厂方向逃去。

“该军官随即指派六名水兵追捕这15人，以防他们逃跑并破坏电厂。该军官留下人员看管其余的人，自己则朝电厂方向走去。此时，纱厂的英国雇员走近水兵，要求移交在厂工作的工人。这一要求被拒绝。随后，这些英国雇员开始与水兵扭打，试图夺走他们的步枪。

“其中一名英国人（廷克勒）向水兵开了一枪，然后朝电厂方向跑去。当他接近负责该小队的日本军官时，他用左手抓住该军官的右前臂，然后将枪抵住该军官，命令他离开工厂。此时，逃跑的罢工者已被那六名水兵在电厂外包围。

所谓行为

“负责该小队的日本军官随即请求增援，与此同时，正准备离开营部前往上海海军陆战队总部的营长收到了厂方的求助请求，称已发生骚乱，需要援助。

“营长随即派出增援部队，于8时10分抵达纱厂，他本人于8时15分抵达。当他到达现场时，那名持枪的英国人连续三次将枪指向营长，同时推搡并威胁要杀死他。此外，他还四处奔跑，用枪指着军官和水兵。

被水兵击打

“鉴于让这样一个手持上膛枪支的人四处乱跑存在危险，一名水兵制服了此人并缴了他的械。正如前述事件所示，陆战队表现出了令人钦佩的耐心，但这名已被缴械的英国人随后扑向该名水兵，企图与其搏斗。

“鉴于这名英国人的袭击行为，另一名水兵抓起他的步枪，用枪托击打了他。此人随后被带往营部。在此之前，厂方经理与驻浦东的日本海军陆战队指挥官之间曾达成谅解，即未经与指挥官达成协议，不得在厂区内使用武器。这是理所当然的，因为陆战队已同意保护该财产。

pages.en:
"The man who discharged the pistol
was named Tinkler, aged 45. In view
of the fact that the Japanese had
agreed to extend full protection to
the property and had taken every
precaution to prevent any damage
to the property, in which they had
been eminently successful, the action
taken by this individual in attacking
members of the Japanese Naval Land-
ing Party must be regarded as a
challenge and consequently as ex-
tremely serious.

Protest Lodged

"Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-
General, at 5 o'clock this afternoon
(Tuesday) called at the British Con-
sulate where he lodged an energetic
protest on this matter. The Consul-
General has also reserved any future
demands on the British authorities."
Immediately after the above state-
ment by the spokesman numerous
questions were asked in connection
with the incident. The spokesman
revealed that Mr. Tinkler had been
treated for his injuries and had
been detained in "protective
custody." He had been able to walk
from the mill to the Battalion Head-
quarters, the spokesman added.
There was no indication when he
would be handed over to the British
authorities. The pistol he had used,
the spokesman continued, had been
fired, as the barrel was dirty and a
cartridge had been found. The action
of the Japanese Commander in order-
ing his men not to fire showed tact
and forbearance and there was no
violence on the part of the Japanese.

Not Yet Arrested

There might have been others
involved, he stated, but Tinkler had
been the principal. Apparently the
others had not attempted to stop him.
Asked if the man's extraterritorial
rights would be respected as the
rights of some Japanese citizens, who
had attacked American marines on
August 13 last, had been respected,
the spokesman stated that this in-
cident could not be considered in the
same light as this man had fired at
a Japanese sailor.
It had not been decided whether he
would be tried by the British auth-
orities or by a Japanese military
tribunal, he continued, as he had not
yet been arrested. At this point a
pressman asked. "An undeclared war,
isn't it?"
All measures to protect the mill
were still being taken, the spokesman
added. No officials were allowed to
visit the man and he would not be
allowed to see anybody until the time
came. The strikers and strikebreakers
had been taken to Company H. Q.
in Pootung.
Asked if it was possible that the
European employees, seeing the
sailors enter the mill, had come
to a mistaken conclusion about
the actions of the sailors, the spokes-
man replied, "They knew what was
going on at the pontoon and that the
Japanese sailors had taken the
fighters. That is not the way to do
it. You don't have to hit a sailor
and take his rifle away from him."
The spokesman added that Tinkler
had shouted "He's the commander.
Let's kill him." Tinkler to say the
least, was trying to antagonize the
Japanese, the spokesman said.
Questioned yesterday afternoon by
the "North-China Daily News" a
British Consular official said that the
incident was being studied and that
an official had been despatched to
Pootung to investigate. They had not
received details of the incident and
these would be forthcoming upon the
official's return.
pages.zh:
“开枪者名为廷克勒，现年45岁。鉴于日本人已同意对该财产提供全面保护，并采取了一切预防措施以防止财产受损，且在这方面取得了显著成效，此人攻击日本海军陆战队成员的行为必须被视为一种挑衅，因而极其严重。

提出抗议

“日本总领事三浦 Y. 先生（Mr. Y. Miura，音译）于今天下午（星期二）5时前往英国领事馆，就此事件提出强烈抗议。总领事还保留向英国当局提出进一步要求的权利。”

在该发言人发表上述声明后，记者们立即就该事件提出了许多问题。发言人透露，廷克勒先生已接受伤势治疗，并被处于“保护性拘留”中。发言人补充说，他能够从纱厂步行至营部。目前尚无迹象表明他何时会被移交给英国当局。发言人继续说，他所使用的手枪已经发射过，因为枪管是脏的，并且发现了一枚弹壳。日本指挥官命令部下不开火的做法显示了机智和克制，日方没有暴力行为。

尚未逮捕

他说，可能还有其他人卷入其中，但廷克勒是主要人物。显然，其他人并没有试图阻止他。当被问及是否会像尊重去年8月13日袭击美国海军陆战队的某些日本公民的权利那样，尊重此人的治外法权时，发言人表示，此事件不能同等看待，因为此人向一名日本水兵开了枪。

他继续说，由于此人尚未被捕，因此尚未决定是由英国当局审判还是由日本军事法庭审判。此时，一名记者问道：“这是一场未宣战的战争，不是吗？”

发言人补充说，保护纱厂的各项措施仍在进行中。不允许任何官员探视此人，在时机到来之前，也不允许他会见任何人。罢工者和顶替者已被带往浦东连部（Company H. Q.）。

当被问及欧洲雇员是否可能因看到水兵进入纱厂而对水兵的行动产生误解时，发言人回答说：“他们知道浮码头发生的情况，也知道日本水兵带走了斗殴者。那不是正确的做法。你不必殴打水兵并从他手中夺走步枪。”

发言人补充说，廷克勒曾喊道：“他是指挥官。让我们杀了他。”发言人称，退一步说，廷克勒是在试图激怒日本人。

《字林西报》记者于昨日下午询问了一位英国领事官员，该官员表示正在研究此事，并已派遣一名官员前往浦东进行调查。他们尚未收到事件的详细情况，待该官员返回后将提供详情。

pages.en:
British Representations

Mr. Tinkler was released through representations made by British Consular authorities who accompanied him on his trip across the Whangpoo. Although no official information was given as to the terms for his release, there were indications that British authorities had tried to make everything clear for future reference before taking the wounded man across the river.

A foreign doctor went to Pootung with the officials and he accompanied Mr. Tinkler on the trip across the river, in the presence of Japanese officers. His presence indicated that Mr. Tinkler was examined by the doctor before he was sent across the river.

Dramatic scenes were witnessed at the Customs Jetty at 11.10 p.m. when the party arrived in a launch. Mr. Tinkler was carried in a stretcher by four Japanese soldiers to the waiting ambulance and in addition to British Consular representatives and police, there were several Japanese officers carrying swords and giving necessary instructions. The stretcher was placed on the ground for a few seconds and then Mr. Tinkler was taken into the ambulance which sped away to the hospital

Mr. Tinkler was covered with a blanket. He looked pale and tired. He turned his head looking around and he could move his hands but he did not talk. Questioned by the reporter at the jetty a foreign colleague of the wounded man said that "he is wounded all right," refusing to give details. After the ambulance had gone the officials said good bye and the Japanese officers and men were seen returning to the launch in the river.
pages.zh:
英国的交涉

廷克勒先生是通过英国领事当局的交涉而被释放的，英国领事官员陪同他穿越黄浦江。虽然没有公布关于其释放条件的官方信息，但有迹象表明，英国当局在将伤者带过河之前，试图为将来参考厘清所有事实。

一名外籍医生随同官员前往浦东，并在日本军官在场的情况下，陪同廷克勒先生渡河。他的在场表明，廷克勒先生在渡河前接受了医生的检查。

晚上11时10分，当一行人乘坐汽艇抵达海关码头时，目睹了戏剧性的场面。廷克勒先生由四名日本士兵用担架抬到等候的救护车上，除了英国领事代表和警察外，还有几名佩剑的日本军官在现场给予必要的指示。担架在地上放置了几秒钟，随后廷克勒先生被送入救护车，迅速驶往医院。

廷克勒先生身上盖着一条毯子。他看起来脸色苍白且疲惫。他转过头环顾四周，双手可以活动，但没有说话。记者在码头询问了一名伤者的外籍同事，该同事称“他确实受伤了”，但拒绝透露细节。救护车离开后，官员们道别，人们看到日本军官和士兵返回河中的汽艇。

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.
JUN 7 1939
14194
45-Year-Old Briton's
Condition Critical
Following Operation
Suffers Three Abdominal
Wounds In Incident
With Japanese
SENTRIES GUARD
OPERATION ROOM
Japanese File Protest;
British Authorities
Are Reticent
Suffering from three abdo-
minal stab wounds, one ser-
ious scalp wound and a badly
bruised right leg, the result
of an experience he had with
the Japanese Naval Landing
Party at Pootung yesterday
morning, Mr. R. M. Tinkler,
45, British, former inspector
of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, was hovering between
life and death in the General
Hospital last night.
He was brought to Shanghai
from Pootung by officers of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party,
accompanied by British Vice-
Consul J. M. Ford and Japanese
Consul A. Uyama, about 11.40
p.m. An emergency ambulance
of the Shanghai Fire Brigade
was waiting for him on the
Settlement side of the river and
he was rushed immediately to
the General Hospital.
Germans Operate
Medical examination made im-
mediately after his arrival at the
hospital revealed that Mr. Tink-
ler's condition was critical where-
upon he was rushed to the operat-
ing room where an emergency
operation was still underway at an
early hour this morning.
Two German surgeons Doc-
tors Koree and Sunhak, and
two Japanese naval doctors
were conducting the operation.
Two Franciscan Sisters were
assisting while two armed
Japanese sentries stood guard
duty directly outside the operat-
ing room door, indication that
the Japanese authorities had
not yet officially handed the
British subject over to the Bri-
tish officials.
Mr. Tinkler was placed on
the operating table about mid-
night and was still undergoing
ether and the knife at 1.30
a.m. It was found that the
stab wounds had punctured the
intestines and he was not ex-
pected to live through the
night.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年6月7日
14194
45岁英国人术后
情况危急
在与日本人发生的事件中
腹部受三处刺伤
哨兵守卫
手术室
日方提出抗议；
英国当局保持沉默

R. M. 廷克勒（Tinkler）先生，45岁，英国人，前上海公共租界工部局警务处巡官，因昨天上午在浦东与日本海军陆战队发生的遭遇，腹部有三处刺伤，头皮有一处严重创伤，右腿严重挫伤，昨晚在公济医院（General Hospital）生命垂危。

他是于晚上11点40分左右，由日本海军陆战队军官护送，在英国副领事 J. M. 福特（Ford）和日本领事 A. 宇山（Uyama，音译）的陪同下，从浦东被带到上海的。上海救火会的一辆紧急救护车在租界一侧的河边等候，他随即被急送往公济医院。

德国医生施行手术
抵达医院后立即进行的医学检查显示，廷克勒先生的情况危急，因此他被紧急送入手术室，直到今天凌晨早些时候，紧急手术仍在进行中。

两名德国外科医生科雷（Koree，音译）博士和孙哈克（Sunhak，音译）博士，以及两名日本海军医生正在实施手术。两名方济各会修女在旁协助，而两名持枪的日本哨兵直接在手术室门外站岗，这表明日本当局尚未正式将该英国臣民移交给英国官员。

廷克勒先生大约在午夜被送上手术台，到凌晨1点30分时仍在接受乙醚麻醉和开刀手术。发现刺伤已穿透肠道，预计他无法熬过今晚。

pages.en:
Mr. Tinkler was injured yesterday
morning during the course of an
incident involving himself and
members of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party at Pootung. The
affair occurred on the premises of
the cotton mill of the China Print-
ing and Finishing Company, Ltd., a
British concern, near Pootung Point
about 8 a.m.
Although the official British ver-
sion of the incident was not released
last night, it was reported in re-
liable circles that Mr. Tinkler was
clubbed with a rifle butt in the
hands of a Japanese soldier after
he had allegedly threatened with a
pistol Japanese naval officers and
sailors said to have been engaged
in breaking up a riot between mill
strikers and strike-breakers.
**British Investigate**
British authorities, questioned by
THE CHINA PRESS last night, stated
that they had nothing to report
other than the fact that a "thorough
investigation of the incident will be
made."
They admitted, however, that
the Japanese consular authori-
ties had lodged a protest with
the British Consul-General. Mr.
Yoshiaki Miura, Japanese Con-
sul-General, called on Sir Her-
bert Phillips, British Consul-
General, at 5 p.m. yesterday and
filed a verbal protest regarding
Mr. Tinkler's alleged action in
"threatening" Japanese officers
and bluejackets with a pistol.
One of two officers "threatened"
was Lieutenant-Commander Mune-
suke Noji, commandant of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party in
Pootung, and the same man who
reported about 10 days ago that
he had been "threatened" by a
Seaforth sentry with a bayonet.

**Ford Crosses River**
British Vice-Consul J. M. Ford,
learning that Mr. Tinkler's condi-
tion was critical, contacted the
Japanese Consulate-General last
night and, accompanied by Japan-
ese Consul A. Uyama, he made the
trip to Pootung. Mr. Ford inter-
viewed Commander Noji. As a re-
sult of this interview, Mr. Tinkler
was placed aboard a launch and
brought to Shanghai.
First intimation that the wounded
man was being brought to Shang-
hai was received on the Settlement
side of the Whangpoo River when
a telephone call came from Poo-
tung requesting the police to have
an emergency ambulance on the
Bund. The call arrived at 10.15
p.m. and the launch reached the
Customs Jetty about one hour and
30 minutes later.
When the ambulance was first
called, attendants were told that
they would proceed to the
Country Hospital with the
wounded man. It is understood,
however, that his condition was
too critical to make the long
trip while at the same time,
Japanese authorities expressed
a desire to have the man sent
to a hospital north of Soochow
Creek.
**Mystery Wounds**
Just how Mr. Tinkler got three
abdominal stab wounds was not
made clear last night. Japanese
reports admitted that a Japanese
sailor had struck the Briton with
a rifle butt in an effort to subdue
the man after he had been disarmed. But the fact remains that he
had three serious stab wounds when
he entered the General Hospital
last night, according to the ambul-
ance report. It also was a fact
that he was held in detention by
Japanese naval authorities at Poo-
tung from about 8.30 a.m. until
almost 11 p.m. yesterday.
pages.zh:
廷克勒先生是在昨天上午浦东发生的一起涉及他本人与日本海军陆战队成员的事件中受伤的。该事件发生在上午8点左右，地点位于浦东角附近的一家英资企业——中国印染整理有限公司（China Printing and Finishing Company, Ltd.）的棉纺厂内。

尽管英国官方昨晚未发布关于此事件的正式说法，但据可靠消息人士透露，廷克勒先生在据称用手枪威胁据信正致力于平息工厂罢工者与破坏罢工者之间骚乱的日本海军军官和水兵后，被一名日本士兵用步枪枪托殴打。

**英国方面展开调查**
《字林西报》昨晚向英国当局询问时，他们表示除了将对“此事件进行彻底调查”这一事实外，无可奉告。

然而，他们承认日本领事当局已向英国总领事提出抗议。日本总领事三浦义明（Yoshiaki Miura）先生于昨天下午5点拜访了英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯（Herbert Phillips）爵士，并就廷克勒先生据称用手枪“威胁”日本军官和水兵的行为提出了口头抗议。

被“威胁”的两名军官之一是驻浦东日本海军陆战队指挥官野路宗助（Munesuke Noji，音译）中佐，此人约在10天前曾报告称自己受到一名海福尔团（Seaforth，音译）哨兵的刺刀“威胁”。

**福特渡江**
英国副领事 J. M. 福特得知廷克勒先生情况危急后，于昨晚联系日本总领事馆，并在日本领事 A. 宇山的陪同下前往浦东。福特先生会晤了野路指挥官。作为此次会晤的结果，廷克勒先生被送上一艘汽艇并带往上海。

关于伤者正被带往上海的最初消息，是在黄浦江租界一侧接到来自浦东的电话时得知的，电话要求警方在外滩安排一辆紧急救护车。电话于晚上10点15分到达，汽艇大约在1小时30分钟后抵达海关码头。

当首次呼叫救护车时，护理人员被告知他们将随伤者前往乡村医院（Country Hospital）。然而据了解，由于他的情况过于危急，无法承受长途跋涉，同时日本当局表示希望将此人送往苏州河以北的一家医院。

**神秘伤口**
廷克勒先生如何造成腹部三处刺伤，昨晚尚不清楚。日方报告承认，一名日本水兵在该英国人被解除武装后，为制服他用步枪枪托击打了他。但事实仍然是，根据救护车报告，他昨晚进入公济医院时身负三处严重刺伤。同样确凿的事实是，他从昨天上午约8点30分到接近晚上11点，一直被日本海军当局拘留在浦东。

pages.en:
Circumstances leading up to Mr.
Tinkler's detention were outlined by
the Japanese naval landing spokes-
man at the regular Japanese press
conference last night. He recalled
that the Japanese Naval Landing
Party in Pootung had agreed to
protect the mill property on May
24, following a request to that effect
by the British consular authorities.
Understanding Said Reached
On May 25, the British soldiers
who were guarding the property
were withdrawn, and on May 27, a
small detachment of Japanese
bluejackets were stationed on the
property. On May 30, the spokes-
man declared, an understanding
had been reached between the Jap-
anese Naval Landing Party and the
management of the mill regarding
protective measures. This accord
had been concluded, the spokesman
stated, in the presence of Major
S. R. Hunt, brigade major of the
British forces in the Shanghai
area, whereupon the Japanese
sailors in the mill had been with-
drawn. A small unit, however, was
maintained near the mill with a
lookout overlooking the property,
he said, adding the Japanese Navy
had gone "out of its way to accord
effective protection to the property."
Japanese Version
"About 7.40 a.m. yesterday," said
the Japanese spokesman, "some 40
millhands—not strikers—arrived at
the mill pontoon." He indicated
that these men were strike-
breakers.
"About 30 mill strikers were wait-
ing in a sampan nearby when they
saw the strike-breakers," he con-
tinued. "The strikers rode to the
pontoon and attacked the workers
with sticks.
"The Japanese landing party
thereupon communicated with the
officer in charge and had about 10
Japanese sailors proceed to the
pontoons to stop the fight. The
sailors jumped over the wall to get
to the pontoon.
"Eventually," continued the Jap-
anese spokesman, "the workers and
strikers were herded together and
escorted by Japanese sailors to the
Japanese Landing Party Headquar-
ters. They passed through the Lun
Chong property approaching the
offices of the mill, and at this point
about 10 Britons appeared from the
mill offices, three of whom were
carrying pistols.
Chase After Strikers
"As they did so," the Japanese
spokesman declared, "about 15 of
the strikers started to run away
from the group of rioters and head-
ed for the power plant of the mill,
whereupon the Japanese officer de-
tailed six of the 10 sailors to pursue
the strikers, both to prevent them
from running away and from caus-
ing damage to the power plant.
"The officer left four sailors in
charge of the rioters and went in
the direction of the power plant.
"At this point," declared the
spokesman, "the 10 British em-
ployees of the mill approached the
four sailors in charge and sought
to take over the rioters.
"A British employee (Tinkler)
wrestled with the sailors in an
attempt to get their rifles," the
Japanese naval spokesman charg-
ed, and then added:
"He hit the sailors and one shot
also was fired at the sailors. The
man (Tinkler) who fired the shot,
ran in the direction of the power
plant and approached the Japanese
officer in charge.
pages.zh:
日本海军陆战队发言人在昨晚的例行日本记者招待会上，概述了导致廷克勒先生被拘留的情况。他回顾说，应英国领事当局的要求，驻浦东的日本海军陆战队已于5月24日同意保护该工厂财产。

据称已达成谅解
5月25日，守卫该财产的英军撤出，5月27日，一小队日本水兵驻扎在该财产内。发言人宣称，5月30日，日本海军陆战队与工厂管理层就保护措施达成了谅解。发言人称，这项协定是在上海地区英军旅参谋长 S. R. 亨特（Hunt）少校的见证下缔结的，随后工厂内的日本水兵即行撤离。然而，他说，在工厂附近保留了一支小部队，并设有瞭望哨监视该财产，并补充说日本海军“不遗余力地为该财产提供有效保护”。

日方版本
日本发言人称：“昨天上午约7点40分，约40名工厂工人——非罢工者——抵达工厂浮码头。”他指出这些人是破坏罢工者。

他继续说道：“当看到破坏罢工者时，约30名工厂罢工者正在附近的一艘舢板上等待。罢工者乘船至浮码头，并用棍棒攻击工人。”

“日本陆战队随即与负责军官取得联系，并派约10名日本水兵前往浮码头制止斗殴。水兵们翻墙跳入以到达浮码头。”

日本发言人继续说：“最终，工人和罢工者被聚集在一起，并由日本水兵护送至日本陆战队总部。他们穿过伦钟（Lun Chong，音译）地产，接近工厂办公室，此时约有10名英国人从工厂办公室出现，其中三人携带手枪。”

追捕罢工者
日本发言人宣称：“当他们这样做时，约15名罢工者开始从暴乱人群中逃跑，朝工厂发电厂方向跑去，于是日本军官指派10名水兵中的6人去追捕罢工者，既是为了防止他们逃跑，也是为了防止他们破坏发电厂。”

“军官留下四名水兵看管暴乱者，自己朝发电厂方向走去。”

发言人宣称：“此时，工厂的10名英国雇员走近负责的四名水兵，试图接管暴乱者。”

日本海军发言人指控：“一名英国雇员（廷克勒）与水兵搏斗，试图夺取他们的步枪，”然后补充道：

“他击打水兵，还有一枪射向水兵。开枪的人（廷克勒）朝发电厂方向跑去，并接近负责的日本军官。”

pages.en:
"Seized Officer's Arm"
"He seized the officer's right fore-arm with his left hand and pressing his gun into the officer's ribs, told him to 'get out of the plant'," the Japanese naval spokesman alleged.
"By this time," continued the spokesman, "the runaway strikers, who had got into the power plant, had been rounded up outside the plant by the six Japanese sailors. Meanwhile, the Japanese officer in charge asked headquarters for reinforcements.
"At the same time," declared the spokesman, "the Japanese battalion commander, who was about to leave Pootung for Shanghai, heard of the trouble at the mill and that help was needed, so he sent reinforcements. These arrived at the mill at 8.10 a.m. while the battalion commander himself arrived at 8.15 a.m.
"When the battalion commander arrived on the scene," asserted the Japanese spokesman, "a British subject (Tinkler), with a gun, pointed his weapon at the battalion commander three successive times, all the while insulting him."
At a later period during the Japanese press conference last night, it was said by the spokesman that Tinkler cried:
"He's the commander. Let's kill him."
The spokesman continued that the British subject, meaning Tinkler, threatened to kill the battalion commander and that he pointed his gun at various other Japanese sailors and officers.

Tinkler Said "Dangerous"
"At this point, the Japanese spokesman started referring to Tinkler as a dangerous character." said he:
"In view of the danger involved in letting a man like that run around with a loaded gun, a Japanese sailor seized the Briton and disarmed him."
"As shown by preceding events," the Japanese spokesman claimed, "the Japanese Naval Landing Party had shown unusual patience, but the disarmed Briton jumped on the sailor and wanted to fight him.
"In view of this assault," continued the spokesman, "another Japanese sailor hit the Briton with the butt of his rifle. The Briton was later taken to Japanese headquarters, where his injury was treated and where he is now being detained in protective custody.
"He was not seriously hurt since he was able to walk to headquarters from the scene of the disturbance," the Japanese spokesman said, and then, as an afterthought, added this illuminating remark: "He is not permitted to see any foreign visitors."

Understanding Claimed
It was at this point that the Japanese spokesman undertook to explain that previously, there had been an understanding between the manager of the plant and the Japanese that no arms were to be used in the plant without Japanese consent.
"In view of the fact that the Japanese naval authorities had agreed to extend full protection to the mill property and had taken unusual precautions to do so," declared the Japanese spokesman, "the action taken by the Briton in attacking a member of the Japanese Naval Landing Party must be regarded as a challenge and as being extremely serious."
pages.zh:
“抓住军官的手臂”
日本海军发言人声称：“他用左手抓住军官的右前臂，将枪顶在军官的肋骨上，命令他‘离开工厂’。”

发言人继续说：“此时，逃入发电厂的罢工者已被六名日本水兵在工厂外包围。与此同时，负责的日本军官向总部请求增援。”

发言人宣称：“同时，正准备离开浦东前往上海的日本营长听说了工厂的麻烦以及需要援助的消息，于是派遣了增援部队。这些部队于上午8点10分抵达工厂，营长本人于上午8点15分抵达。”

日本发言人断言：“当营长抵达现场时，一名英国臣民（廷克勒）持枪，连续三次将武器指向营长，期间一直对其进行侮辱。”

在昨晚日本记者招待会的稍后阶段，发言人称廷克勒喊道：
“他是指挥官。让我们杀了他。”
发言人继续说，这名英国臣民，即廷克勒，威胁要杀死营长，并将枪指向其他几名日本水兵和军官。

廷克勒被称为“危险人物”
“此时，日本发言人开始称廷克勒为危险人物。”他说：
“鉴于让这样的人携带装有子弹的手枪四处游荡所涉及的危险，一名日本水兵抓住了这名英国人并解除了他的武装。”

日本发言人声称：“如前事所示，日本海军陆战队表现出了异乎寻常的耐心，但这名被解除武装的英国人扑向水兵，想与他打斗。”

发言人继续说：“鉴于这次袭击，另一名日本水兵用步枪枪托击打了这名英国人。该英国人后来被带到日本总部，在那里接受了伤势治疗，目前正被保护性拘留。”

日本发言人说：“他没有受重伤，因为他能够从骚乱现场步行到总部，”随后，像是事后补充般，加了这句发人深省的话：“他不允许会见任何外国访客。”

声称已有谅解
正是在这一点上，日本发言人试图解释此前，工厂经理与日方之间已有谅解，未经日方同意，不得在工厂内使用武器。

日本发言人宣称：“鉴于日本海军当局已同意对工厂财产提供全面保护，并采取了不同寻常的预防措施，该英国人攻击日本海军陆战队成员的行为必须被视为一种挑衅，且性质极其严重。”

Incidentally, the officer involved
in this affair is Lieutenant Com-
mander Munesuke Noji, command-
ant of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party in Pootung, and the same
officer who accused a Seaforth sen-
try of having wounded him with a
bayonet recently.
... goes without saying that the
sensational statement made by the
Japanese naval spokesman tonight
brought forth a barrage of questions
from the foreign newsmen present.
In answering these questions, the
spokesman declared that "there is
no indication that Tinkler will be
handed over to the British at the
present time."

Pistol Seized

He also stated that there was
nothing to indicate that Tinkler's
breath smelled of liquor at the
time of the incident. But he did
maintain that the pistol Tinkler
used was seized and that the barrel
indicates that it had been fired. He
also claimed that the cartridge case
had been found.
No confirmation could be obtained
from other sources tonight that
a shot actually had been fired by
Tinkler.
The most important question raised
by the newsmen was whether or
not Mr. Tinkler's extraterritorial
rights will be respected.
"They will be taken into consideration," the spokesman declared.
"Will they be taken into consideration in the same way as the
United States Marines respected the
Japanese extraterritorial rights
when, on last August 13, Japanese
were taken into custody?" a correspondent wanted to know.

"Not In Same Light"

"They cannot be discussed in the
same light," said the spokesman
tersely, although a Japanese member of the special service section
threatened Sergeant "Slug" Marvin,
of the 4th U.S. Marines when the
incident of last August 13 occurred.
"Will Mr. Tinkler be brought before a Japanese military tribunal
or turned over to the British
authorities for questioning?" another foreign correspondent inquired.
"That has not yet been decided,"
the spokesman replied.
Regarding Mr. Tinkler's extraterritorial rights, the Japanese spokesman said that "the possibility of
his rights not being respected was
a difficult question since Tinkler
has not yet been arrested, but is
only being detained in protective
custody."
It was at this point that one
foreign correspondent piped up with
the brilliant remark that this might
be something "like an undeclared
war."

"Treatment Different"

Continuing, the spokesman said
that "when the time comes Tinkler
will be allowed to see visitors. At
present he is not being permitted to
see anyone."
In answer to a correspondent who
asked whether refusal to permit
Tinkler to see anyone isn't "like
arrest," the spokesman replied that
the "treatment is entirely different."
Also being held at Japanese Naval
Landing Party headquarters in
Pootung tonight are the workers
and strikers involved in the scrap
on the pontoon yesterday morning
—the original rioters. But there are
no Japanese troops at the Lun
Chong Mill at present, the spokesman added.
In conclusion, the Japanese
spokesman voiced his own private
opinion that "probably Tinkler is a
very vicious individual."

顺便提一下，卷入此事的军官是驻浦东日本海军陆战队指挥官野路宗助（Munesuke Noji）中佐，也就是最近指控一名海福尔团（Seaforth）哨兵用刺刀刺伤他的同一名军官。
……不言而喻，日本海军发言人今晚发表的耸人听闻的声明，引发现场外国记者的一连串提问。在回答这些问题时，该发言人宣称，“目前没有任何迹象表明廷克勒（Tinkler）将被移交给英方。”

手枪被缴

他还表示，没有任何迹象表明事件发生时廷克勒呼出的气息带有酒味。但他确实坚持称，廷克勒使用的手枪已被缴获，且枪管显示其曾被发射过。他还声称发现了弹壳。
今晚无法从其他来源获得证实，证明廷克勒确实开过枪。
记者提出的最重要问题是，廷克勒先生的治外法权是否会得到尊重。
“我们会予以考虑，”发言人宣称。
“会像去年8月13日美军尊重日本人治外法权、拘捕日本人时那样予以考虑吗？”一位记者想知道。

“不能相提并论”

“不能相提并论，”发言人简短地说道，尽管在去年8月13日事件发生时，特务科的一名日本成员曾威胁美国海军陆战队第四团的“斯勒格”（Slug）马文（Marvin）军士。
“廷克勒先生会被送上日本军事法庭，还是移交给英国当局进行讯问？”另一位外国记者问道。
“那尚未决定，”发言人回答。
关于廷克勒先生的治外法权，日本发言人表示，“由于廷克勒尚未被捕，只是处于保护性拘留中，因此其权利可能得不到尊重这一问题是个难题。”
就在此时，一名外国记者插话发表了一句高见，称这可能有点像“不宣而战”。

“待遇不同”

发言人接着说，“当时机成熟时，将允许廷克勒会见访客。目前他不允许见任何人。”
针对一名记者提出的不允许廷克勒见任何人是否“如同逮捕”的问题，发言人回答说，“待遇完全不同”。
昨晚在浦东日本海军陆战队总部被扣留的还有昨天上午在浮桥上发生冲突的工人和罢工者——即最初的暴乱分子。但发言人补充说，目前伦钟纱厂内没有日军。
最后，日本发言人表达了他个人的看法，认为“廷克勒很可能是一个非常凶恶的人”。

JUN 7 1939
Briton Succumbs
To Stab Wounds
In Pootung Clash
OPERATION FAILS
TO SAVE COTTON
MILL EMPLOYEE
Lun Chong Official Dies In Hospital
Mr. R. M. Tinkler died in the General Hospital
at 5.30 a.m. today.
Brought to the hospital last night from Pootung
by two members of the British Consulate-General staff,
he was found to be suffering from two bayonet wounds
in the abdomen which had caused many wounds in the in-
testines and bowels and a haemorrhage. He had lost a great
deal of blood and had small chance
from the first.
Dr. W. Korce, German, and
Dr. Reidar Sundsbak, Nor-
wegian, performed the operation,
assisted by three Japanese sur-
geons.
Fight In Pootung
A former inspector of the
Shanghai Municipal Police, and
holder of a British Distinguished
Conduct Medal for gallantry
during the Great War, when he
served in the Royal Fusiliers, Mr.
Tinkler was a native of Grange-
over-Sands in Lancashire. He
had been in the employ of the
China Printing and Finishing
Company for some years, and was
45 years of age.
His wounds were received yes-
terday in the course of a fight at
the Pootung Point plant of his
firm, where a strike has been in
progress for some days. Some
sort of a scrap broke out yester-
day afternoon in which the
Japanese allege Mr. Tinkler fired
a pistol at an officer of the Japan-
ese Naval Landing Party, who
had guaranteed to the British
authorities that they would pro-
tect the place.
Bayonet Wounds
The Japanese disarmed Mr.
Tinkler, but it is not known whe-
ther they bayonetted him before
disarming him or afterwards. His
wounds included one in the scalp
and another in the leg.
Japanese authorities at first re-
fused to hand Mr. Tinkler over
to the British authorities, but
finally he was allowed to be
brought to Shanghai.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》
（午版）
1939年6月7日
英国人在浦东冲突中
因刺伤身亡
手术未能挽救
棉厂员工性命
伦钟厂官员在医院去世
R. M. 廷克勒先生于今日凌晨5时30分在广慈医院去世。
昨晚由英国总领事馆两名工作人员从浦东送至医院后，发现他腹部有两处刺刀伤，导致肠道多处受伤并出血。他失血过多，从一开始生还希望就很渺茫。
德国医生W. Korce和挪威医生Reidar Sundsbak实施了手术，三名日本医生协助。

浦东斗殴
廷克勒先生是兰开夏郡格兰奇奥弗桑兹（Grange-over-Sands）人，曾任上海公共租界工部局警务处巡官，并在第一次世界大战期间服役于皇家燧发枪团时因英勇表现获得英国杰出行为勋章。他受雇于中国印染整理公司已有数年，享年45岁。
他的伤口是在昨天其公司位于浦东点的工厂发生的斗殴中受的，该工厂的罢工已持续数日。昨天下午爆发了某种冲突，日方指控廷克勒先生向一名日本海军陆战队军官开枪，该军官曾向英国当局保证他们会保护该地。

刺刀伤
日方解除了廷克勒先生的武装，但不知他们是在解除武装之前还是之后用刺刀刺伤了他。他的伤口包括头皮一处和腿部一处。
日本当局起初拒绝将廷克勒先生移交给英国当局，但最终允许将其送往上海。

（批：No.）
（批：C%）

Pootung Mill
Hands Openly
Blame Puppets
“City Gov’t” Agents
Said Deliberately
Fostering Strike
How striking workers of the
Lun Chong Cotton Mill in Poo-
tung were prevented from re-
turning to their work on June
5 by alleged agents of the
“Shanghai City Government”
was set forth in a letter sent
to a local Chinese daily yester-
day by representatives of the
workers.
Following the amicable settlement
between the disputing parties, the
letter stated, a large number of
workers arrived at the factory on
the morning of May 29 to report to
work but discovered that “puppet
agents” had already been posted
near the entrances around the
compound.
The workers’ attempts to gain ad-
mittance into the factory, the letter
added, were forcibly resisted by
these agents, while Japanese troops
who patrolled the area for the
alleged purpose of protecting the
property against trespassing strik-
ers, stood by without interfering.
Keep Close Watch
For several days following the
June 5 effort to return to work,
puppet agents in large numbers
were stated to have kept a day and
night watch around the factory so
that workers who arrived as early
as 5 o’clock in the morning were
prevented from entering their place
of employment.
During the many melees between
workers and puppet agents, the
former, according to the letter,
sustained several casualties. Rumors
were also spread around the plant
that if work should be resumed, the
agents would rush the factory com-
pound and forcibly halt operations.
Asserting that the workers were
in a destitute condition, the letter
urged “the kind public” to mediate
on their behalf so that they might
again return to employment.
Anti-British Activities
Meanwhile, the bogus regime in
Shanghai continued its efforts to
stir up anti-British sentiments
with the organization of the “New
Shanghai Anti-British League” in
Pootung. Over the week-end, several
parades of workers and hired
loafers were staged, while parti-
cipants distributed thousands of
anti-British leaflets.
Entrances to both the new and
old plants of the British-owned
factory were still guarded by
Japanese soldiers and puppet police
and as a result, workers could not
enter the plant.
“Agents” At Waterfront
Along the riverfront of the factory,
members of the “workers’ or-
ganization” were stationed to
scrutinize any workers who at-
tempted to get near the entrance.
Another report stated that Chinese
workers, numbering about 80, who
were arrested by Japanese troops
during the Thakler incident last
Tuesday had been released.
As a condition of release, the
workers were forced to promise
that they would not return to the
factory for the duration of the
strike, the report added.
（批：Liu）
（批：C 13/6）
（批：R 13/6）

浦东工厂
公开指责傀儡
“市政府”特工
称故意煽动罢工

工人代表昨日致信当地一家中文日报，阐述了浦东伦钟棉厂的罢工工人如何被所谓的“上海市政府”特工阻止在6月5日复工。
信中指出，在争议双方达成友好和解后，大批工人于5月29日上午到达工厂报到上班，却发现“傀儡特工”已经部署在厂区周围的入口附近。
信中补充说，工人们试图进入工厂的努力遭到这些特工的武力抵抗，而据称为了保护财产免受罢工者侵入而在该地区巡逻的日军则袖手旁观，未加干涉。

严密监视
据称，在6月5日尝试复工后的几天里，大量傀儡特工日夜监视工厂周围，致使早在早上5点到达的工人无法进入工作场所。
信中说，在工人与傀儡特工发生的多次混战中，前者遭受了数人伤亡。厂区内还散布谣言称，如果复工，特工们将冲进厂区，强行停止作业。
信中断言工人处于贫困境地，敦促“仁慈的公众”代表他们进行调解，以便他们能重新就业。

反英活动
与此同时，上海的伪政权继续通过在浦东组织“新上海反英联盟”来煽动反英情绪。上周末，举行了数次由工人和受雇闲散人员参加的游行，参与者分发了数千份反英传单。
这家英资工厂的新旧厂房入口仍由日本士兵和伪警察把守，因此工人无法进入工厂。

水边的“特工”
沿工厂河岸，“工人组织”的成员 stationed 在那里，仔细盘查任何试图靠近入口的工人。
另一份报告称，上周二在廷克勒（Thakler）事件中被日军逮捕的大约80名中国工人已被释放。
报告补充说，作为释放的条件，工人们被迫承诺在罢工期间不再返回工厂。
（批：Liu）
（批：C 13/6）
（批：R 13/6）

据我们收到的报告称，浦东的反英示威者正从其赞助者那里获得丰厚的报酬。支付给每个示威者的金额各不相同，但据告诉我们，每一个愿意加入反对英国及英国利益运动的人，都会得到某种形式的金钱补偿。有一份报告称，劳工每月获得30美元，以不为英国工厂工作。

Miura Given
British Note
On Agitators

Consul General Affirms
Verbal Protest In
Pootung Acts

ELIMINATION OF
ARMED MEN ASKED

Strong Complaint Made
On Expressions In
Sin Shun Pao

Confirming his verbal representations Thursday morning to Mr. Yoshiaki Miura, Japanese Consul-General, Sir Herbert Phillips, British Consul-General here, on Friday addressed an official note to Mr. Miura, it was learned yesterday.

The note, as did the verbal representations which preceded it, and which were exclusively reported by THE CHINA PRESS Friday, referred to the presence of armed Japanese plainclothesmen in the immediate neighborhood of the China Printing and Finishing Company's print works at Pei Lien Ching Creek in Pootung.

These bands, it was stated, had intimidated Chinese laborers desiring to resume work following the settlement of the strike. They also fired on two members of the company's British staff who had appeared outside the works with a view to encouraging the workers' return.

Cause Plant To Close

As a result of this unmolested activity of the armed bands, the note pointed out, it has been found necessary to close the print works altogether for the time being.

The written protest also requested the suppression of armed bands and agitators operating in the vicinity of the print works, and also the full protection by Japanese armed forces of the British staff still residing at the company's print works and cotton mill at Pootung Point.

The suppression of the activities of agitators near the Pootung Point mill, and the cessation of at present widely-spread anti-British agitation and propaganda, also were requested in the note.

（批：Liu R 12/6）

1939年6月11日
14373
6968 B
4 6 31

三浦收到
英国照会
谈及煽动者

总领事确认
就浦东行为
提出口头抗议

要求清除
武装人员

就《新顺报》言论
提出强烈抗议

据悉，英国驻沪总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）于周五向日本总领事三浦义明（Yoshiaki Miura）先生递交了一份正式照会，确认了他周四上午向三浦先生所作的口头交涉。

该照会与此前的口头交涉一样，提及了在浦东北莲泾（Pei Lien Ching Creek）中国印染整理公司印刷厂附近地区存在武装日本便衣人员的情况。此前的口头交涉已由《字林西报》在周五独家报道。

据称，这些团伙恐吓了在罢工解决后希望复工的中国劳工。他们还向两名出现在工厂外、旨在鼓励工人返岗的公司英籍职员开枪。

导致工厂关闭

照会指出，由于这些武装团伙不受干扰的活动，目前不得不完全关闭印刷厂。

书面抗议还要求镇压在印刷厂附近活动的武装团伙和煽动者，并要求日本武装部队对仍居住在浦东点公司印刷厂和棉厂的英籍职员提供全面保护。

照会还要求镇压浦东点棉厂附近煽动者的活动，并停止目前广泛传播的反英煽动和宣传。

（批：Liu R 12/6）

14374

Propaganda Hit
The protest asked for the preven-
tion of anti-British processions and
parades in Pootung, and of the
affixing of posters and distribution
of literature of an anti-British
nature.
The suppression of anti-British
organizations, such as the Ta Min
Hui, was also requested in the note.
Of particular interest is that the
note for the first time officially
directed the attention of the Jap-
anese authorities to anti-British
agitation here in the Japanese-con-
trolled Chinese-language newspaper,
the Sin Shun Pao.
Referring to an article which
appeared in the Sin Shun Pao last
Wednesday, the note charged that
its publication constituted a virtual
incitement to violence against Bri-
tish interests. The appearance of
this article, it was noted, was held
by the British Consulate-General
as particularly unfortunate insofar
as it appeared the day after the
events which led to the tragic death
of Mr. Richard Maurice Tinkler.

Recalls British Action
Sir Herbert pointed to efforts
which British authorities had made
to suppress anti-Japanese propagan-
da in the British-owned Chinese
press here, and requested that Mr.
Miura reciprocate by taking similar
action with regard to the Japanese-
controlled Sin Shun Pao.

It will be recalled that on May
18 the British Consulate-General
suspended two British-owned Chin-
ese papers, the Wen Hui Pao and
the Yih Pao, for two weeks.

The article published in the Sin
Shun Pao referred to Britons as
men who had come to China "with
the ambition of robbers ... their
aim to squeeze price of labor to fill
their pockets." It also advised
against any settlement of the Lun
Chong Cotton Mill strike, present-
ing its view that compromise meant
total destruction.

Attention was directed to the
Canton-Hongkong strike of 1927,
and an appeal was made to workers
to "follow the spirit of the Canton
workers" in overthrowing "British
imperialism in China."

British Protest
(Havas)
LONDON, June 10.—A new pro-
test has been forwarded to Tokyo
by His Majesty's Government in
connection with the events which
brought about the death of Mr.
R. M. Tinkler, an employee of the
British Finishing and Printing Co.
in Shanghai, it was officially stated
here today.
pages.zh:
14374

宣传攻势

抗议要求防止在浦东举行反英游行和集会，以及张贴和分发具有反英性质的海报和宣传品。

照会中还要求取缔大民会（Ta Min Hui）等反英组织。特别引人关注的是，该照会首次正式提请日本当局注意由日本人控制的中文报纸《新顺报》（Sin Shun Pao）在此地进行的反英煽动活动。

照会提及上周三刊登在《新顺报》上的一篇文章，指责该文的发表实际上构成了对针对英国利益的暴力行为的煽动。据指出，英国总领事馆认为这篇文章的发表尤为不幸，因为它出现在导致理查德·莫里斯·廷克勒先生（Mr. Richard Maurice Tinkler）悲剧性死亡的事件发生的次日。

回顾英国的行动

赫伯特爵士（Sir Herbert）指出，英国当局曾努力压制在上海由英国拥有的中文报刊中的反日宣传，并要求三浦先生（Mr. Miura）采取对等措施，对日本人控制的《新顺报》采取类似行动。

需指出的是，5月18日，英国总领事馆暂停了两家英资中文报纸《文汇报》（Wen Hui Pao）和《益报》（Yih Pao）的出版，为期两周。

《新顺报》发表的这篇文章称英国人是怀着“强盗般的野心”来到中国的人，“他们的目的是压榨劳动力价格以填满自己的口袋”。文章还反对任何解决伦钟棉纺厂罢工的做法，提出其观点认为妥协意味着彻底毁灭。

文中提到了1927年的省港大罢工，并呼吁工人“追随广州工人的精神”，推翻“在中国的英国帝国主义”。

英国抗议
（哈瓦斯社）
伦敦，6月10日电。——今日此处官方宣布，陛下政府已就导致上海英国整理印刷公司（British Finishing and Printing Co.）雇员R. M. 廷克勒先生死亡的事件，向东京发出新的抗议。

CHINA PRESS.
JUN 1 1 1939

London Said Drafting
New Note Rejecting
Nippon Demands
BRITISH REPRISALS
BELIEVED CERTAIN
May Present Claims For
Compensation On
Tinkler Death
(United Press)
LONDON, June 10.—Tension
between Britain and Japan con-
tinued to mount today as the
British Government was reported
drafting a new note to Japan
flatly denying Japanese claims to
the right to dominate the ad-
ministration of foreign settle-
ments in China.
The note, which was under con-
sideration last week but delayed
pending a clarification of Japan's
intentions, probably will be worded
in unmistakable terms and leave
no doubt in Japanese Government
circles that further Japanese at-
tacks on British interests and na-
tionals in China will meet with
British reprisals, it was understood.
Tinkler Protest
The British Foreign Office dis-
closed that the protest handed
Japanese authorities in Shanghai
yesterday against the "unjustified"
bayonet attack on the late Mr.
R.M. Tinkler reserved Britain's
right to present claims for com-
pensation.
Japanese interference with Bri-
tish business interests in China,
the Japanese blockade of the China
coast, the anti-British campaign
sponsored by Japan throughout
Japanese occupied territory and
the "limitation" of rights of British
nationals in China by Japan were
said to be driving the British Gov-
ernment toward a policy of retalia-
tion.
pages.zh:
14372
《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）
1939年6月11日

据悉伦敦正在起草
拒绝日本要求的新照会
相信英国必将
采取报复行动
可能就廷克勒
死亡事件提出
赔偿要求
（合众社）
伦敦，6月10日电。——据报道，英国政府正在起草一份给日本的新照会，断然否认日本有权主宰中国外国租界的行政管理权，英日之间的紧张局势今日继续升级。

据悉，该照会上周已在审议中，但因等待澄清日本的意图而推迟，预计将以毫不含糊的措辞行文，使日本政府各界毫无疑问地认识到，日本进一步攻击在华英国利益和英国国民将招致英国的报复。

廷克勒事件抗议

英国外交部披露，昨日向上海日本当局提交的关于已故R.M.廷克勒先生遭受“无正当理由”刺刀袭击的抗议书，保留了英国提出赔偿要求的权利。

据说，日本干涉英国在华商业利益、日本封锁中国海岸、日本在整个日军占领区赞助的反英运动，以及日本对英国在华国民权利的“限制”，正促使英国政府走向报复政策。

JUN 1 1 1939
New Protest Over Death
Of R. M. Tinkler
London, June 10.
A new protest has been forwarded to Tokyo by His Majesty's Government in connection with the events which brought about the death of Mr. R. M. Tinkler, an employee of the China Printing and Finishing Co. in Shanghai, it was officially stated here today.—Havas.

《字林西报》（NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS）
1939年6月11日

就R. M. 廷克勒之死
提出新抗议

伦敦，6月10日。
今日此处官方宣布，陛下政府已就导致上海中国整理印刷公司（China Printing and Finishing Co.）雇员R. M. 廷克勒先生死亡的事件，向东京发出新的抗议。——哈瓦斯社。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
14367
JUN 1 1 1939

Armed Gang Intimidates Men
At British Factory

Written Protest Made by Consulate Against
Action in Pootung ; Propaganda Control Asked

IN confirming his verbal representations made the previous day,
Sir Herbert Phillips, British Consul-General addressed a
strongly-worded Note to the Japanese Consul-General on June 9,
it was officially learned yesterday.
The Note referred to the presence of armed bands in the im-
mediate vicinity of the China Printing and Finishing Co.'s plant
at Pei Lien Ching, who had intimidated workers trying to resume
work following settlement of the strike. Two members of the
British staff of the plant were also fired upon by these bands,
according to the Note, when they appeared outside the works
with a view to encouraging the workmen to return. As a result
of these intimidations, the Note continues, the Chinese employees
had been unable to return to their work so that the owners of
the plant were forced to close down altogether for the time being.

The suppression of these armed
bands and agitators operating in the
vicinity of the printing works, as
well as the protection of British
members of the staff, was also de-
manded. Furthermore, the suppres-
sion of agitators operating in the
vicinity of the Pootung Point mill,
was requested.
The Note also referred to the pres-
ent anti-British agitation and pro-
paganda at Pootung and demanded
that this be stopped. The prevention
of anti-British parades and the affix-
ing of anti-British posters was also
demanded in the Note, whilst a re-
quest was made that anti-British or-
ganizations such as the Ta Min Hui,
be suppressed.

Anti-British Article
Attention is also drawn to the
anti-British article which appeared
in the "Sin Shun Pao", Japanese-
owned Chinese language daily, on
June 7 and in this connection H.M.
Consul-General referred to the
efforts which the British authorities
had made in suppressing all anti-
Japanese propaganda in British-own-
ed Chinese-language newspapers.
The Japanese Consul-General was
requested to take a similar action
in connection with the "Sin Shun
Pao".
The article to which the British
Consul-General refers, and which,
according to the Note, contains a
virtual incitement to violence against
British interests, was regarded as
particularly unfortunate inasmuch as
it was published the day following
the events which led to Mr. R. M.
Tinkler's death as a result of bay-
onet-wounds sustained at the hands
of Japanese bluejackets.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》（NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS）
14367
1939年6月11日

武装团伙恐吓
英国工厂员工

领事馆就浦东行为
提出书面抗议；要求
控制宣传

据昨日官方获悉，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）于6月9日向日本总领事发出了一份措辞严厉的照会，以确认其前一天所作的口头交涉。

照会提及，在北莲泾（Pei Lien Ching）的中国整理印刷公司工厂附近出现了武装团伙，他们恐吓那些在罢工解决后试图复工的工人。照会称，当两名该厂的英籍职员出现在厂外，旨在鼓励工人返工时，也遭到了这些团伙的枪击。照会继续指出，由于这些恐吓行为，华籍员工无法返回工作岗位，致使工厂业主被迫暂时完全停工。

照会还要求镇压在印刷厂附近活动的这些武装团伙和煽动者，并保护英籍职员。此外，还要求镇压在浦东角（Pootung Point）纱厂附近活动的煽动者。

照会还提及目前在浦东进行的反英煽动和宣传活动，并要求予以停止。照会还要求防止反英游行和张贴反英海报，同时要求取缔大民会（Ta Min Hui）等反英组织。

反英文章

提请注意6月7日在日本人拥有的中文日报《新顺报》（Sin Shun Pao）上发表的反英文章，在此方面，英国总领事提及英国当局在压制英资中文报纸中所有反日宣传方面所做的努力。

已请求日本总领事就《新顺报》采取类似行动。

英国总领事所指的那篇文章，据照会称，包含了对针对英国利益的暴力行为的实际煽动，鉴于该文发表于导致R. M. 廷克勒先生因被日本水兵刺伤致死的事件次日，因此被认为尤为不幸。

pages.en:
14368

Tension Increases
London, June 10.
Tension between Britain and Japan continued to mount today as the British Government was reported drafting a new vote to Japan flatly denying Japanese claims to the right to dominate the administration of foreign settlements in China.
The Note, which was under consideration last week but delayed pending a clarification of Japan's intentions, probably will be worded in unmistakable terms and leave no doubt in Japanese Government circles that further Japanese attacks on British interests and nationals in China will meet with British reprisals, it was understood.
The British Foreign Office disclosed that the protest handed the Japanese authorities in Shanghai yesterday against the "unjustified" bayonet attack on the late Mr. R. M. Tinkler reserved Britain's right to present claims for compensation.
Japanese interference with British business interests in China, the Japanese blockade of the China coast, the anti-British campaign sponsored by Japan throughout Japanese-occupied territory and the "limitation" of rights of British nationals in China by Japan were said to be driving the British Government toward a policy of retaliation.—United Press.

14368

紧张局势加剧

伦敦，6月10日。
据报道，英国政府正在起草一份给日本的新照会（原文误作vote，应为note），断然否认日本有权主宰中国外国租界的行政管理权，英日之间的紧张局势今日继续升级。

据悉，该照会上周已在审议中，但因等待澄清日本的意图而推迟，预计将以毫不含糊的措辞行文，使日本政府各界毫无疑问地认识到，日本进一步攻击在华英国利益和英国国民将招致英国的报复。

英国外交部披露，昨日向上海日本当局提交的关于已故R. M. 廷克勒先生遭受“无正当理由”刺刀袭击的抗议书，保留了英国提出赔偿要求的权利。

据说，日本干涉英国在华商业利益、日本封锁中国海岸、日本在整个日军占领区赞助的反英运动，以及日本对英国在华国民权利的“限制”，正促使英国政府走向报复政策。——合众社。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
JUN 8 1900

Lun Chong Loses
Second Briton
Within 24 Hours

Hector McAllister Dies
After Collapsing
In Pootung

AUTOPSY SLATED
FOR AFTERNOON

Evidence Of Foul Play
Not Discovered
At Hospital

Second British member of the Lun Chong Pootung Point staff to die within the day following the death of Mr. R. M. Tinkler, from bayonet wounds, Mr. Hector Mc-Allister passed away last night.

In this case there are no signs of stab wounds or bruises, and at present his death remains a mystery. Dr. I. G. Anderson is to perform an autopsy this after-noon, following which the Bri-tish Court Coroner will decide whether to hold an inquest.

Sitting At Table
Mr. McAllister was found last night sitting at a table at the China Printing and Finishing Company's cotton factory, slumped up and motionless. Other mem-bers of the foreign staff examin-ed him, and decided to rush him to Shanghai.

Brought across by launch, Mr. McAllister was rushed by a fire department emergency ambulance to the Country Hospital, reaching there shortly after 11.30 p.m., when Dr. W. Korek examined him and pronounced him dead. It is be-lieved that Mr. McAllister had been dead for over half an hour when he arrived at the hospital.

Excitement
While at present there is no in-dication as to how Mr. McAllister died, it is thought possible that the reason was heart failure occasion-ed by the excitement of the clash in which Mr. Tinkler received his fatal wounds, coupled with the hot and humid weather.

A native of Lancashire, Mr. McAllister was 35 years of age. He had joined the Lun Chong staff six years ago.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮与信使报》（SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY）
1900年6月8日 [注：原文年份疑似OCR错误，结合上下文应为1939年]

伦钟厂24小时内
失去第二名
英国人

赫克托·麦卡利斯特
在浦东昏倒后
去世

定于下午
进行尸检

医院未发现
他杀迹象

继R. M. 廷克勒先生因刺刀伤去世后，伦钟浦东角厂 staff 中第二名在一天内死亡的英籍成员赫克托·麦卡利斯特先生（Mr. Hector McAllister）于昨晚去世。

在此案中，没有刺伤或瘀伤的迹象，目前他的死因仍是个谜。I. G. 安德森医生（Dr. I. G. Anderson）将于今天下午进行尸检，随后英国法庭验尸官将决定是否举行死因调查。

坐在桌旁

昨晚发现麦卡利斯特先生坐在中国整理印刷公司棉纺厂的一张桌子旁，瘫软不动。其他外籍职员检查了他，并决定急忙将他送往上海。

麦卡利斯特先生由快艇载过江，由消防队急救救护车紧急送往乡村医院（Country Hospital），于晚上11点30分过后不久到达，W. 科雷克医生（Dr. W. Korek）对他进行了检查并宣布其死亡。据信，麦卡利斯特先生到达医院时已死亡超过半小时。

骚动

虽然目前尚无迹象表明麦卡利斯特先生是如何死亡的，但人们认为可能的原因是，在廷克勒先生受致命伤的那次冲突中受到的惊吓，加上炎热潮湿的天气，导致了心力衰竭。

麦卡利斯特先生是兰开夏郡人，享年35岁。他于六年前加入伦钟厂工作。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JUN 8 1929

Plainclothesmen Firing
In Pootung Intimidation

Firing shots in the air to discourage workers of the Lun Chong
printing plant from returning to work, 50 troops of the Japanese-
sponsored Pootung regime, wearing civilian clothes, demonstrated yes-
terday morning. A further demonstration took place this morning.
These fifty mixed in with Pootung riff-raff, apparently in support
of an anti-British agitation. All this took place at the Pal Lien Ching
Creek plant of the China Printing and Finishing Company, close to
the Robert Dollar Wharf, and it is reported that one bystander, not
a member of the Lun Chong staff, was wounded yesterday morning
and had to be taken to hospital in Nantao.
This plant is not that at which Mr. R. M. Tinkler was fatally
wounded by bayonets of Japanese sent to guard British property. Mr.
Tinkler was wounded at the Pootung Plant cotton factory of the firm.
The British Consulate-General has not yet protested officially to
the Japanese authorities over the killing of Mr. Tinkler, but a careful
study of the whole affair is now being made. A Japanese version of
Mr. Tinkler's death, offered at the Japanese press conference yester-
day, said that Mr. Tinkler received his bayonet wounds when he
ran into the bayonets of Japanese naval sentries.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮与信使报》（SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY）

1929年6月8日 [注：原文年份疑似OCR错误，结合上下文应为1939年]

便衣人员在浦东
开枪恐吓

昨天上午，50名身穿便服的日本支持的浦东政权部队，向空中开枪，以阻止伦钟印刷厂的工人回去工作。今天上午又发生了一次类似的示威活动。

这五十人与浦东的流氓无赖混在一起，显然是在支持反英煽动活动。这一切都发生在靠近罗伯特·多尔码头（Robert Dollar Wharf）的中国整理印刷公司北莲泾（Pal Lien Ching Creek）工厂，据报道，昨天上午有一名旁观者（非伦钟厂员工）受伤，不得不被送往南市医院。

该工厂并非R. M. 廷克勒先生被派去保卫英国财产的日本士兵用刺刀致命刺伤的地方。廷克勒先生是在该公司的浦东工厂棉纺厂受伤的。

英国总领事馆尚未就廷克勒先生被杀一事向日本当局提出正式抗议，但目前正在仔细研究整个事件。在昨天的日本新闻发布会上，日方对廷克勒先生之死的说法称，廷克勒先生是在撞上日本海军哨兵的刺刀时受到刺伤的。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JUN 8 1939

Setting A Fire
ON THE MORNING that Mr. R. M. Tinkler
died at the General Hospital of wounds
suffered as result of strike trouble at the
British-owned China Printing and Finishing
Company in Pootung Point, an inflammatory
editorial concerning this strike was published
by the Japanese-sponsored Chinese language
newspaper Sin Shun Pao.
In view of the great delicacy of mind
registered by the Shanghai Municipal Council
concerning even routine news reports in the
Occidental-owned Chinese language press, we
feel it may be a real service to call attention to
the fact that the Sin Shun Pao seized this
moment to denounce the ownership of the
company in question as a spearhead of British
imperialism, coming to China "with the
ambition of robbers... their aim to squeeze the
price of labor to fill their pockets."
The editorial in question argued against
negotiation of the present trouble or any sort
of agreement, declaring that compromise meant
total destruction.
Attention was called to the Canton-Hong-
kong strike of a decade ago and workers at the
Chinese plant were urged to "follow the spirit
of fellow-workers in Canton" in overthrowing
"British imperialism in China."
There is of course nothing new of all this.
It has been going on constantly in all ter-
ritories under Japanese military domination.
But since the Council is out for moderation on
the part of the Chinese language press, and
since we ourselves wholeheartedly subscribe to
the policy of peace, order and international
fellowship in trying times, we believe it may be
serviceable to point out that free circulation in
the foreign areas is being accorded an organ
whose whole policy appears to be to stir up
trouble for Japan's partners in Settlement con-
trol particularly Great Britain.
As to what is being done among the Ja-
panese community by that precious organ the
Tairiku Shimpo, most readers of the daily
press are in position to judge for themselves
by the translations daily printed. A recent
one refers to Britons at the printing plant as
"uneducated hoodlums" whose "impertinence
and violence represents the contempt and en-
mity of Britons as a whole towards Japan"—a
lying statement in its every aspect, and one
for which it is most regrettable that no legal
recourse is available.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》。

1939年6月8日

纵火案
就在 R. M. 廷克勒（R. M. Tinkler）先生因在浦东角英商中国印染公司罢工纠纷中受伤，于总医院去世的那天早晨，一家由日本人资助的中文报纸《新顺报》发表了一篇关于此次罢工的煽动性社论。
鉴于上海公共租界工部局对西人拥有的中文报刊甚至常规新闻报道所表现出的极度敏感心态，我们认为，指出《新顺报》利用这一时机谴责该公司业主为英国帝国主义先锋的事实，或许能提供一种真正的服务，称其“怀着强盗般的野心……来到中国”，其目的是“压榨劳动力价格以填满自己的口袋”。
该社论反对就目前的纠纷进行谈判或达成任何形式的协议，宣称妥协意味着彻底毁灭。
文中提请注意十年前的省港大罢工，并敦促该中国工厂的工人“效仿广州同仁的精神”，推翻“在华的英国帝国主义”。
当然，这些都不足为奇。在日本军事统治的所有领土上，这种情况一直在不断发生。但是，既然工部局力求中文报刊保持克制，而且我们自己也全心全意赞同在艰难时期实行和平、秩序和国际友好的政策，我们相信，指出一个其全部政策似乎旨在为租界管理中的日本伙伴、特别是英国制造麻烦的机构正在外侨区域自由流通，或许是有益的。
至于那份珍贵的刊物《大陆新报》在日本社群中做了什么，大多数日报读者可以通过每天刊登的译文自行判断。最近的一篇译文将印刷厂的英国人称为“未受教育的流氓”，称其“无礼和暴力代表了全体英国人对日本的蔑视和敌意”——这是一种彻头彻尾的谎言，令人遗憾的是，对此无法采取法律手段。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, JUN 15 1939
14565
No. S. H. P. 69687
15 / 39
Wounds Eight to Ten Inches
Long in Mr. Tinkler's Body
Inquest Reveals Infliction of Five Stab
Wounds ; Dragged for About Thirty Yards

WOUNDS from eight to ten inches in length had been discovered
as the result of a post mortem examination conducted on the
body of the late Mr. Richard Maurice Tinkler, labour superinten-
dent of the China Printing & Finishing Co.'s Lun Chong mill at
Pootung Point, who had died as the result of injuries sustained
during a fight with Japanese marines at the mill premises on
June 6, it was revealed in H. M. Coroner's Court yesterday after-
noon when the inquest was resumed by Mr. C. H. Haines, H. M.
Coroner. Also revealed was the fact that Mr. Tinkler had been
bayonetted during a struggle with the Japanese marines at the
mill and had been dragged by them about thirty yards before
being allowed to walk.

Present at the enquiry were Mr.
H. H. Thomas, H.M. Consul for
Japanese Affairs; and Mr. John Mc-
Neill, who was instructed by the
China Printing & Finishing Co. on
behalf of the next of kin of de-
ceased and on behalf of the firm.
The first witness, Dr. Wladimir
Korec of 110 Szechuen Road, told
the Coroner that at about 11 p.m. on
June 6 he was called to the Japan-
ese Military Hospital in Pootung
and was conveyed there by launch.
Here he saw Tinkler, who appeared
to be in "a very bad state." He was
perspiring profusely, and was in a
cold sweat, witness added. In addi-
tion his hands were cold and he was
almost without pulse.
"I looked at him and I gained the
impression," Dr. Korec continued,
"that he was suffering from very bad
internal injuries. His body and some
parts of his clothes were covered in
blood and there was only one hope
for him—an immediate operation to
repair the internal injuries as far as
possible." Tinkler, he stated, was
taken to a launch on a stretcher by
Japanese marines and was conveyed
to the Customs Jetty. From there he
was removed to the General Hospi-
tal by ambulance, witness having
gone on ahead to see that every-
thing was prepared.

Bleeding Badly

Tinkler arrived at the hospital at
about 11.40 p.m., Dr. Korec told the
Coroner, and an operation was com-
menced in the presence of his part-
ner Dr. Sunsbak, and two Japanese
surgeons from the Naval Landing
Party who, later, were joined by
another Japanese surgeon in uni-
form. "We opened the abdomen and
on examining the intestines from the
stomach to the end we found several
perforations in the small intest-
ines," he said. "I closed the per-
forations and then there were some
other injuries in that part where the
small intestines are. There was some
blood from the sub-arteries in the
tissue which holds the small intest-
ines."
After stating that the sub-arteries
had been closed Dr. Korec explained
that inside the abdominal cavity he
found liquid and coagulated blood.
During the operation, he added, the
patient was bleeding very badly and
he had the impression that he would
expire on the table. Saline and
glucose were administered to assist
the function of the heart, 1½ litres
being given to the man.
The operation finished at about
2.15 a.m. on June 7 and at that time
Tinkler had very little pulse. At
5.30 the same morning he died.
Answering the Coroner Dr. Korec
said that Tinkler had a lacerated
wound on the head, and above the
right hip there was a wound in the
skin which had perforated the ab-
dominal wall. A similar wound was
on the left side of the body under
the rib while the hands and forearm
were covered with bruises.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1939年6月15日
14565
编号 S. H. P. 69687
15 / 39
廷克勒先生身上有八至十英寸长的伤口
死因裁判官法庭揭示其遭受五处刺伤；被拖行约三十码

昨天下午，在英国驻华死因裁判官 C. H. 海恩斯（C. H. Haines）先生主持恢复的死因裁判官法庭上揭示，在对位于浦东角的中国印染公司伦钟厂劳工主管理查德·莫里斯·廷克勒（Richard Maurice Tinkler）先生的遗体进行尸检后，发现其身上有长达八至十英寸的伤口，他于6月6日在该厂址与日本海军陆战队士兵打斗中受伤致死。法庭还揭示，廷克勒先生在与日本海军陆战队士兵搏斗期间被刺刀刺伤，并在被允许行走之前被他们拖行了约三十码。

出席调查的有日本事务英国领事 H. H. 托马斯（H. H. Thomas）先生；以及约翰·麦克尼尔（John McNeill）先生，他受中国印染公司指示，代表死者近亲属及该公司行事。
第一位证人，四川路110号的弗拉基米尔·科雷茨（Wladimir Korec）博士告诉死因裁判官，6月6日晚上11点左右，他被召往浦东的日本陆军医院，并由汽艇送往那里。在那里，他看到了廷克勒，后者看起来“状况非常糟糕”。证人补充说，他大汗淋漓，浑身冷汗。此外，他的双手冰凉，脉搏几乎消失。
“我查看了他，得到的印象是，”科雷茨博士继续说道，“他遭受了严重的内伤。他的身体和部分衣物沾满了鲜血，对他来说只有一线希望——立即进行手术，尽可能修复内伤。”他说，廷克勒被日本海军陆战队士兵用担架抬上汽艇，并被运往海关码头。随后，他被救护车送往总医院，证人则先行前往以确保一切准备就绪。

严重出血

科雷茨博士告诉死因裁判官，廷克勒大约在晚上11点40分到达医院，手术在他的合伙人桑斯巴克（Sunsbak）博士以及两名来自海军登陆部队的日本外科医生在场的情况下开始，后来又有一名身穿制服的日本外科医生加入。“我们切开腹部，检查从胃到末端的小肠时，发现小肠上有几处穿孔，”他说。“我缝合了穿孔，然后发现小肠所在部位还有其他一些损伤。固定小肠的组织中的小动脉有一些出血。”
在说明小动脉已被结扎后，科雷茨博士解释说，他在腹腔内发现了液体和凝固的血液。他补充说，在手术过程中，病人出血非常严重，他给人的印象是他会死在手术台上。为了帮助心脏功能，给予了盐水和葡萄糖，向该男子输入了1.5升液体。
手术于6月7日凌晨2点15分左右结束，当时廷克勒的脉搏非常微弱。同一天早上5点30分，他去世了。
回答死因裁判官的提问时，科雷茨博士说，廷克勒头部有一处撕裂伤，右髋上方皮肤有一处伤口，穿透了腹壁。左侧肋骨下方身体部位也有类似的伤口，而双手和前臂布满瘀伤。

pages.en:
Early Treatment Necessary
The Coroner—Had these injuries
been treated?
Dr. Korec—Only one was treated
superficially.
This was the wound on the right
side where the skin had been
stitched up. When I removed the
stitches to investigate plenty of
blood poured out from the wound.
There was a small bandage around
his head.
Asked if earlier treatment would
have saved Tinkler's life, Dr. Korec
stated "All the medical and surgical
books state that the earlier an opera-
tion is performed in such a case
the better the chance of recovery. In
my opinion he would have had a
very good chance of recovery had
there been an early operation, especi-
ally as all the injuries were in the
small intestines which are much less
infectious than the large."
Dr. Ian George Anderson, in de-
scribing a post mortem examination
he had made on Tinkler's body at
the General Hospital on June 7,
stated that he had conducted this in
the presence of Dr. Korec, Dr.
Sundsbak, Dr. Hertz and a Japanese
doctor. His report, which was handed
to the Coroner, revealed that there
had been bruising on the left arm
and shoulder, right forearm and
hand and on the right leg. There
were also drag marks on his back
which had caused bruising and
abrasions.

Five Stab Wounds
Tinkler had sustained one stab
wound on the right flank of the
abdomen, one stab wound on the
left flank of the abdomen, on the
right buttock, the right thigh and in
the abdomen. These wounds in the
abdomen were eight to ten inches
in length. The term bayonet wounds
was fit to describe these injuries the
report stated.
An internal examination had
revealed that there were two stab
wounds in the abdominal cavity and
many perforations in the intestines.
Peritonitis was commencing around
the wounds and the cause of death
was shock and haemorrhage due to
stab wounds in the abdomen. In
all there were five stab wounds, the
report stated, all of them probably
having been caused by the same
instrument or the same type of
instrument. To cause the damage
that they did considerable force
must have been used. Answering the
Coroner, Dr. Anderson stated that
the marks on Tinkler's back were
consistent with his having been
dragged along the ground.

Shot Fired
William Brankin, a clerk employed
by the China Printing & Finishing
Co. at the Lun Chong mill, told the
Coroner that at about 8 a.m. on
June 6 he was looking out of the
bathroom window and he noticed
several Japanese marines running to
the company's pontoon where there
was a band of Chinese, several of
whom appeared to be armed with
sticks.
The Chinese, witness continued,
were marched by the Japanese
through the gateway and into the
mill compound where they were
halted about ten yards from the
office buildings. Immediately they
stopped several of the Chinese dash-
ed towards the power house, witness
going to his room to get dressed and
go downstairs to see what was hap-
pening.
The next thing he saw was Mr.
Tinkler coming out from the flats
with a Mauser pistol in his hand
walking towards the Japanese and
Chinese. Witness again went back
into his room and just as he was
about to go downstairs again he looked
through the window and saw Tinkler
struggling with two Japanese mar-
ines. During this struggle he fired
a shot.
14568
pages.zh:
早期治疗至关重要
死因裁判官——这些伤口得到处理了吗？
科雷茨博士——只有一处得到了 superficially（表面）处理。
这是右侧的伤口，皮肤已被缝合。当我拆线检查时，大量血液从伤口涌出。他的头上缠着一个小绷带。
当被问及早期治疗是否能挽救廷克勒的生命时，科雷茨博士表示：“所有医学和外科学书籍都指出，在这种情况下，手术越早进行，康复的机会就越大。在我看来，如果尽早进行手术，他会有很好的康复机会，尤其是因为所有伤势都在小肠，其感染性远小于大肠。”
伊恩·乔治·安德森（Ian George Anderson）博士在描述他于6月7日在总医院对廷克勒遗体进行的尸检时表示，他是在科雷茨博士、桑德斯巴克（Sundsbak）博士、赫茨（Hertz）博士和一名日本医生的见证下进行此项检查的。他提交给死因裁判官的报告揭示，其左臂和肩膀、右前臂和手以及右腿均有瘀伤。他的背部还有拖拽痕迹，导致瘀伤和擦伤。

五处刺伤
廷克勒腹部右侧肋 flank 处有一处刺伤，腹部左侧肋 flank 处有一处刺伤，右臀部、右大腿和腹部各有一处刺伤。报告称，腹部的这些伤口长达八至十英寸。报告指出，“刺刀伤”一词适合描述这些伤害。
内部检查显示，腹腔内有两处刺伤，肠道有多处穿孔。伤口周围开始出现腹膜炎，死因是由于腹部刺伤导致的休克和出血。报告称，总共有五处刺伤，所有这些伤口可能都是由同一器械或同类型器械造成的。要造成这样的损害，必须使用了相当大的力量。回答死因裁判官时，安德森博士表示，廷克勒背部的痕迹与他被拖行在地面上相符。

开枪
威廉·布兰金（William Brankin），中国印染公司伦钟厂的一名职员，告诉死因裁判官，6月6日上午8点左右，他正从浴室窗户向外看，注意到几名日本海军陆战队士兵跑向公司的浮码头，那里有一群中国人，其中几人似乎手持棍棒。
证人继续说，中国人被日本人驱赶穿过大门，进入工厂大院，在距离办公楼约十码的地方停下。他们刚一停下，几名中国人就冲向发电房，证人回到房间穿衣服并下楼查看发生了什么事。
他接下来看到的是，廷克勒先生手里拿着一支毛瑟手枪，从公寓楼走出来，走向日本人和中国人。证人再次回到房间，就在他准备再次下楼时，他透过窗户看到廷克勒与两名日本海军陆战队士兵扭打在一起。在这场搏斗中，他开了一枪。
14568

pages.en:
14567

At the Ground
Describing the firing of the shot Mr. Brankin explained that Tinkler held one of the Japanese marines off with his left hand while he turned away and fired at the ground. He then walked away towards the offices. When witness got downstairs he was ten or fifteen yards away from the offices while in the doorway were four other foreign employees—H. McAllister, W. F. Allen, A. M. Raskin, and Robitchek. At this time Japanese reinforcements were arriving.
Three other employees, J. Sharples, W. V. K. Chadwick and H. Stott, at this time were standing near the Japanese. "As the Japanese reinforcements were arriving Tinkler seemed to get angrier than ever," Mr. Brankin went on, and on occasions he pointed his pistol at the marines and officers. On each occasion either Chadwick or Sharples appeared to try and persuade him to adopt a more reasonable attitude. The Japanese then loaded their guns and surrounded the office buildings."

Bayonets Fixed
Bayonets were then fixed, he continued, and about ten others surrounded Tinkler, Sharples, Stott and Chadwick. After sometime Tinkler was disarmed by a marine, who jumped on his back and knocked his pistol to the ground. Tinkler tried to grab it but several of the Japanese commenced to beat him with their rifles and he was hit both with bayonets and the rifle butts. I saw him on the ground once and the Japanese still appeared to be beating him. He then got to his feet, and Sharples and Chadwick rushed in amongst the Japanese trying to push them on one side," witness stated.
"A few seconds later I saw Tinkler being dragged out by a crowd of Japanese and he appeared to be bleeding badly—his shirt was covered in blood at the time. Chadwick shouted for three of us to go and help him and three people made an attempt to go but were ordered to stop by the Japanese. Tinkler was dragged along the ground for about 30 yards towards the back of the mill. Sharples and Chadwick followed behind. The next time I saw Tinkler he was walking."
The Coroner—You are quite certain that he pointed his gun at the ground?
Witness—I'm positive, sir. He did not point the gun at anybody. Two marines were close to him and the next one was about ten yards away.
pages.zh:
14567

朝地面开枪
描述开枪情景时，布兰金先生解释说，廷克勒用左手挡住一名日本海军陆战队士兵，同时转身朝地面开枪。然后他朝办公室方向走去。当证人下楼时，他距离办公室十到十五码远，门口还有另外四名外籍雇员——H. 麦卡利斯特（H. McAllister）、W. F. 艾伦（W. F. Allen）、A. M. 拉斯金（A. M. Raskin）和罗比切克（Robitchek）。此时，日本增援部队正在抵达。
另外三名雇员 J. 夏普尔斯（J. Sharples）、W. V. K. 查德威克（W. V. K. Chadwick）和 H. 斯托特（H. Stott）当时站在日本人附近。“随着日本增援部队的到来，廷克勒似乎变得比以往任何时候都更加愤怒，”布兰金先生继续说道，有时他会用手枪指向海军陆战队士兵和军官。每次出现这种情况，查德威克或夏普尔斯似乎都试图劝说他采取更理性的态度。随后日本人给枪支装上子弹，包围了办公楼。”

装上刺刀
他继续说，随后日军装上了刺刀，大约十名其他人包围了廷克勒、夏普尔斯、斯托特和查德威克。过了一会儿，廷克勒被一名跳到他背上并将他的手枪打落在地的海军陆战队士兵缴械。廷克勒试图去抓枪，但几名日本人开始用步枪殴打他，他被刺刀和枪托击中。我看到他倒在地上一次，日本人似乎仍在殴打他。然后他站了起来，夏普尔斯和查德威克冲进日本人中间，试图将他们推开，”证人陈述道。
“几秒钟后，我看到廷克勒被一群日本人拖走，他似乎流血严重——当时他的衬衫上沾满了血。查德威克大喊让我们三个人去帮忙，三个人试图过去，但被日本人喝令停止。廷克勒被沿着地面拖行了约30码，朝向工厂后方。夏普尔斯和查德威克跟在后面。我下一次看到廷克勒时，他正在行走。”
死因裁判官——你完全确定他是朝地面开枪的吗？
证人——我十分肯定，先生。他没有把枪指向任何人。两名海军陆战队士兵离他很近，下一名大约在十码之外。

pages.en:
14568

Mouth Bleeding

John Sharples, spinning supervisor
at the mill, stated that at about 8
a.m. on June 6 he was having break-
fast in the dining room when there
was a commotion on the pontoon.
Later he looked through a window
on the South side and saw a band
of coolies going in the direction of the
power house. There were also two
Japanese marines, who were "walking
leisurely behind in the same direc-
tion."

At this period, he stated, Stott was
also looking through the window and
witness informed him that he was
going to get a gun. "We both ran
upstairs to Tinkler's room and asked
him for a gun each. He gave Stott
the keys to the box and at the same
time he was preparing his own
Mauser," Sharples continued. "Stott,
having opened the box, they each
took a gun while witness secured 15
rounds of ammunition. While they
were doing this Tinkler left the room
and witness was the last to leave.

"I ran towards the office buildings
where the trouble was taking place,"
he stated, "and about half-way there
I heard a shot. When I arrived at
the spot where the Japanese and Chi-
nese were I saw that this group con-
tained a number of Number Ones,
clerks and maintenance men and then
Chadwick arrived and we tried to
explain to a Japanese, who appeared
to be an N.C.O., that these were loyal
people. Tinkler then arrived from the
direction of the mill and I noticed
that his mouth was bleeding. He had
his gun drawn."

At this stage Mr. Haines adjourned
the inquest until 10 a.m. today.
pages.zh:
14568

口部出血

该厂纺纱主管约翰·夏普勒斯（John Sharples）称，6月6日上午8时许，他正在餐厅吃早餐，此时浮桥上发生骚动。随后，他透过南侧的一扇窗户向外张望，看见一群苦力朝发电厂方向走去。还有两名日本海军陆战队员，“在同一方向上悠闲地走在后面”。

他说，在此期间，斯托特（Stott）也在透过窗户观望，证人告知斯托特他要去取枪。“我们俩都跑上楼到廷克勒（Tinkler）的房间，向他每人要一支枪。他把箱子的钥匙给了斯托特，同时他自己也在准备他的毛瑟手枪，”夏普勒斯继续说道。“斯托特打开箱子后，他们各取了一支枪，而证人则拿了15发子弹。在他们做这些事的时候，廷克勒离开了房间，证人是最后离开的。”

“我朝发生骚乱的办公大楼跑去，”他说，“跑到半路时，我听到一声枪响。当我到达日本人和中国人所在的地方时，我看到这群人中有许多‘一号’（Number Ones，注：指高级职员或头等职员）、文员和维修工，随后查德威克（Chadwick）赶到，我们试图向一名看似是士官的日本军人解释，这些都是忠诚的人。这时廷克勒从工厂方向赶来，我注意到他嘴里在流血。他拔出了枪。”

在此阶段，海恩斯先生（Mr. Haines）宣布验尸听证会休庭，直至今天上午10点继续。

SHANGHAI TIMES,
14592
JUN 1 5 1939
Municipality Official To
Mediate In Mill Strike
Representatives Of Lun Chong Mill, Strikers, Gather
In Meeting At Office Of Mr. Chu Yu-chen;
10 Demands Made By 3,700 Workers
Acting upon a request for
mediation, said to have been made
by the China Printing and Finish-
ing Company, proprietors of the
strike-bound Lun Chong textile
mills in Pootung, subsequently
matched by the strikers, Mr. Chu
Yu-chen, director of the political
affairs bureau of the South Pootung
Ward Office of the Special Muni-
cipality of Shanghai, yesterday
afternoon called a meeting in his
office between the embattled Bri-
tish employers and their Chinese
workers, Japanese newspapers re-
ported yesterday evening.
Representing the operators of the
plants at this meeting, the news-
papers said, were Dr. D. J. Sin-
clair, and two others, while the
workers were represented by two
men and one woman.
The Lun Chong firm, on June 10,
the Shanghai "Mainichi" reported,
suddenly abandoned its attitude of
disregarding the de facto author-
ities of Pootung and sought Mr.
Chu's mediation. The latter de-
clined to act unless the same re-
quest were made by the strikers.
When these also asked him to
mediate, he agreed, the newspaper
reported.
A set of 10 demands allegedly
made by the 3,700 strikers at the
firm's two plants were to form the
basis for negotiation, the "Mainichi"
stated.
The main difficulty in reaching an
agreement, the "Tairiku Shimpo"
said, would be the question of the
workers alleged by the company to
have instigated the strike. The
Lun Chong side, the newspaper
understood, wanted to dismiss
them.

《上海泰晤士报》，
14592
1939年6月15日
市政府官员将调解纱厂罢工
伦钟纱厂代表与罢工者聚集在朱裕珍先生办公室开会；
3700名工人提出10项要求

据日本报纸昨晚报道，上海特别市南浦东区公署政治事务局局长朱裕珍先生于昨日下午在其办公室召集了处于对峙状态的英国雇主与中国工人举行会议。此举是应据说由位于浦东、因罢工而陷入困境的伦钟纺织厂业主中国印染整理公司（China Printing and Finishing Company）提出的调解请求，随后罢工者也提出了同样的请求。

报纸称，出席此次会议的资方代表为D. J. 辛克莱博士（Dr. D. J. Sinclair）及另外两人，而工人方面则由两男一女作为代表。

据上海《每日新闻》（Mainichi）报道，伦钟公司于6月10日突然改变了无视浦东事实当局的态度，寻求朱先生的调解。后者表示，除非罢工者也提出同样的请求，否则他将不予介入。据该报报道，当罢工者也请求他调解时，他同意了。

《每日新闻》称，据称该公司两家工厂的3700名罢工工人提出的一套10项要求，将构成谈判的基础。

《大陆新报》（Tairiku Shimpo）称，达成协议的主要困难在于公司指控煽动罢工的工人处理问题。据该报了解，伦钟方面希望解雇这些工人。

14561
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
JUN 15 1939

Shanghai Troubles in
House of Commons
Japanese Said Connected
With Mill Strikes

London, June 14.
In reply to a question in the House
of Commons today by Mr. Adrian
Moreing, Conservative member for
Preston, Mr. R. A. Butler, Under-
Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs.
said that, as a result of anti-British
agitation, a number of strikes recently
had occurred in British-owned fac-
tories situated in the neighbourhood
of Shanghai.
The strikes, Mr. Butler added, had
occurred outside the International
Settlement.
The agitation, he went on, appear-
ed to have been directed by the
Japanese-sponsored Chinese adminis-
tration in Pootung. There was rea-
son to believe that certain Japanese
elements were actively connected
with it.
Representations, Mr. Butler contin-
ued, had been made both to the local
Japanese authorities, and to the
Japanese Government in Tokyo, re-
questing that early steps be taken to
put a stop to the activities in question.
Mr. Moreing asked if it were not
a fact that parties had been organ-
ized by the Japanese Government to
proceed to British mills, and to sup-
port and encourage industrial dis-
putes; and if, as a consequence, dis-
putes had arisen which were not ac-
tually bona fide strikes, but had been
fomented by the Japanese authori-
ties.
Mr. Butler replied that he had given
the facts as brought to the attention
of Lord Halifax.—Reuter.

14561
《字林西报》，
1939年6月15日

上海骚乱引发英国下议院关注
称日本人与纱厂罢工有关

伦敦，6月14日电。
针对保守党普雷斯顿选区议员阿德里安·莫林先生（Mr. Adrian Moreing）今日在下议院提出的问题，外交部次长R. A. 巴特勒先生（Mr. R. A. Butler）回答说，由于反英煽动，近期在上海附近的英资工厂发生了一系列罢工。

巴特勒先生补充说，这些罢工发生在国际租界之外。

他接着说，这种煽动似乎是由日本支持的浦东中国行政当局所指挥。有理由相信，某些日本分子积极参与其中。

巴特勒先生继续说，已向当地日本当局以及东京的日本政府提出交涉，要求尽早采取措施制止上述活动。

莫林先生询问，日本政府是否组织人员前往英国纱厂，支持并鼓励劳资纠纷；以及由此引发的纠纷是否并非真正的罢工，而是由日本当局煽动的。

巴特勒先生回答说，他已陈述了提请哈利法克斯勋爵（Lord Halifax）注意的事实。——路透社。

JUN 10 1939
14339
6968 A
12 6 31

British Protest Made in Death
Of Mr. R. M. Tinkler

Unnecessary Infliction of Bayonet Wounds, and Delay
In Affording Medical Attention Stressed in Note

STRESSING the fact that the bayonet wounds inflicted by Japanese sailors on Mr. Richard Maurice Tinkler, labour superintendent of the China Printing & Finishing Co.'s Lum Chong mill, on Tuesday morning had been unnecessary and were the result of his death at the General Hospital on Wednesday morning, British Consular authorities lodged a strong protest with the Japanese authorities yesterday afternoon in connection with the man's death. Strongly worded, the protest referred to the failure of the Japanese authorities to provide adequate medical attention and their refusal to allow British officials to see the badly-injured man.

In the note the following points were noted, the "North-China Daily News" was informed yesterday:
1. The unnecessary infliction of bayonet wounds which had resulted in Tinkler's death.
2. The failure of the Japanese authorities to make arrangements for adequate medical attention which might have saved his life.
3. The refusal of the Japanese authorities to allow the British Consular authorities to see Tinkler on the afternoon of June 6, and their refusal to allow a foreign doctor to be sent until many hours had elapsed, despite official and verbal requests for this purpose.

At the Japanese Press Conference yesterday, the Embassy spokesman stated that on Thursday Sir Herbert Phillips, H.M. Consul-General had called on Mr. Miura, Japanese Consul-General, and protested against the anti-British movements in Japanese-controlled Pootung and requested Japanese co-operation in suppressing it.

Questioned on the Japanese attitude, the spokesman stated that due attention will be paid to Sir Herbert's request.

A correspondent suggested that the Japanese were in a position, having armed men in that area, to suppress the anti-British demonstrations, should they desire, to which the spokesman retorted that due attention would be given the strikers—even in England the authorities were squeamish about interfering in matters of capital and labour, and the present circumstances made the situation very difficult.

"If there is only a political tinge—capital and labour not being involved —will the Japanese prevent anti-British meetings; they are capable of doing so."

"Your question is delicately phrased," replied the spokesman "As long as peace and order are maintained, there probably will be no interference."

Funeral at Hungjao Cemetery

"At present Might Is Right" was the inscription on one of the numerous beautiful floral tributes seen at the funeral yesterday afternoon of the late Mr. Tinkler, at the Hungjao cemetery. The large number of persons awaiting the arrival of the coffin, indicated the popularity which the late Mr. Tinkler had enjoyed here.

About 20 members of the United Services Association Shanghai, of which the deceased had been a member, were present and eight from amongst them, acted as pall-bearers, whilst all of them wore their medals. The coffin, which was covered with the Union Jack and a wreath of poppies from the U.S.A. was then carried to the graveside where Dean Trivett officiated whilst many of those present were considerably moved as the coffin was lowered to its last resting place.

就廷克勒先生之死提出英国抗议

照会强调不必要的刺刀伤害及延误提供医疗救治

英国领事当局昨日下午就中国印染整理公司伦钟纱厂劳工主管理查德·莫里斯·廷克勒先生（Mr. Richard Maurice Tinkler）之死，向日本当局提出强烈抗议，强调周二上午日本水兵对廷克勒先生造成的刺刀伤害是不必要的，且正是导致其周三上午在总医院死亡的原因。这份措辞严厉的抗议照会指出，日本当局未能提供充分的医疗救治，并拒绝让英国官员探视这名重伤员。

据昨日获悉，《字林西报》得知照会中指出了以下几点：
1. 造成廷克勒死亡的不必要的刺刀伤害。
2. 日本当局未能安排可能挽救其生命的充分医疗救治。
3. 尽管有官方和口头请求，日本当局仍拒绝在6月6日下午允许英国领事当局探视廷克勒，并在数小时后才允许派遣外籍医生。

在昨日的日本记者招待会上，使馆发言人表示，周四英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）拜访了日本总领事三浦先生（Mr. Miura），就日本控制下的浦东地区的反英运动提出抗议，并要求日本方面合作予以镇压。

当被问及日本方面的态度时，发言人表示将对赫伯特爵士的请求给予适当关注。

一名记者暗示，如果愿意，日本人凭借在该地区拥有的武装人员，有能力镇压反英示威，对此发言人反驳说，将对罢工者给予适当关注——即使在英国，当局在干预资本与劳工事务上也颇为顾忌，目前的局势使得情况非常棘手。

“如果仅仅带有政治色彩——而不涉及资本与劳工关系——日本人是否会阻止反英集会？他们是有能力这样做的。”

“您的提问措辞很微妙，”发言人回答，“只要维持和平与秩序，可能就不会进行干预。”

虹桥公墓葬礼

“强权即公理”（At present Might Is Right）是昨日下午在虹桥公墓举行的已故廷克勒先生葬礼上看到的众多精美花圈挽联中的一条题词。大量等候灵柩到来的人群，表明已故廷克勒先生在此地深受爱戴。

死者生前所属的上海联合服务协会（United Services Association Shanghai）约有20名成员出席，其中8人担任护柩者，所有人都佩戴着勋章。覆盖着英国国旗和来自美国的罂粟花花圈的灵柩随后被抬至墓穴旁，特里维特教长（Dean Trivett）主持仪式，当灵柩缓缓降入最后的安息之地时，在场的许多人深受感动。

（批注：档案 1/6）

CHINA PRESS.
JUN 10 1939

Second British
Protest Now
Being Prepared

British consular authorities are
preparing another written protest
to be delivered within the next few
days to the Japanese Consulate-
General, THE CHINA PRESS learned
yesterday. The protest will confirm
verbal representations made by Sir
Herbert Phillips to Mr. Yoshiaki
Miura Thursday morning dealing, as
exclusively reported by THE CHINA
PRESS yesterday, with the Japanese
fosterage of anti-British agitation in
Pootung.
The endorsement by Japanese
armed forces of anti-British labor
agitation in Pootung was protested
verbally by Sir Herbert, it will be
recalled, shortly before the King's
birthday reception at the British
Consulate-General Thursday morn-
ing.
On that occasion, Sir Herbert
pointed to the action of armed
Japanese plainclothesman early
Thursday morning in interfering
with British-employed Chinese
labor.
The British Consul-General re-
quested Mr. Miura to take such
steps as would be found necessary
to prevent the recurrence of such
activity by Japanese. He referred
to an incident which occurred at
the Lun Chong printing plant at
the Pai Lien Ching Creek in Poo-
tung, close to the Robert Dollar
Wharf.
On this occasion, armed Japanese
plainclothesmen prevented laborers
from returning to the British-
owned printing plant to work, al-
though the strike had already been
settled.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）。
1939年6月10日

英国现正
准备第二次抗议

据《字林西报》昨日获悉，英国领事当局正准备另一份书面抗议书，将于未来数日内递交日本总领事馆。该抗议书将确认赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）于周四上午向三浦义明先生（Mr. Yoshiaki Miura）所作的口头交涉。正如《字林西报》昨日独家报道，该交涉涉及日本在浦东煽动反英 agitation（骚动/煽动）一事。

回想起来，赫伯特爵士曾在周四上午英国总领事馆举行的英王寿辰招待会前不久，就日本武装部队支持浦东反英劳工骚动一事提出口头抗议。

在那次场合，赫伯特爵士指出了周四清晨武装日本便衣人员干涉受雇于英国人的中国劳工的行为。

英国总领事要求三浦先生采取必要措施，防止日本人再次发生此类活动。他提及发生在浦东白莲泾（Pai Lien Ching Creek）、靠近罗伯特·多尔码头（Robert Dollar Wharf）的伦钟印刷厂（Lun Chong printing plant）的一起事件。

在此次事件中，尽管罢工已经解决，但武装日本便衣人员仍阻止劳工返回这家英资印刷厂工作。
