随后看来，日方成功制止了斗殴，将打斗者聚集在一起，并着手将他们带入工厂。据日方报告称，就在此时，三名手持手枪的外国人出现并试图干预。他们显然是该工厂的雇员，其中一人据称是丁克勒（Tinkler）先生。随后究竟发生了何事，尚待证实。目前看来，死者曾在日方面前挥舞手枪，并被指侮辱了一名日本军官。日方报告还声称，死者也开了一枪。

接下来发生了什么？
从那一刻起，对于随后发生的情况似乎存在一些疑点。死者显然被缴了械，并遭到步枪枪托的殴打。他腹部的三处刺刀伤是否是在当时造成的，尚不清楚。无论如何，他在周二深夜被送往公济医院（General Hospital）时，腹部伤势严重，医学界人士称，这些伤口及随后的失血导致了他的死亡。

继周二上午的骚乱以及丁克勒先生被带往日本海军陆战队浦东办事处之一后，英国当局获悉了此事。据悉，一名英国领事代表试图与伤者取得联系，但未获日方许可。可靠消息称，该领事官员被告知，丁克勒先生并无危险，其伤势并不危急。英国当局提出接管丁克勒先生的提议未被接受，当天余下时间里探视伤者的所有努力均告徒劳。

得知病情危重
直到周二晚上约10点钟，英国领事馆和伦昌纱厂（Lun Chong Mill）管理层才获悉丁克勒先生病况严重。随即安排派遣一名外籍医生前往浦东，德国外科医生W. Korec博士乘专用汽艇前往那里。安排了将丁克勒先生运往上海的事宜，他用担架被抬上一艘日本汽艇，于晚上11点左右抵达上海一侧。随后他被送往公济医院，接受了数小时的手术，最终于昨日凌晨5点前不久不治身亡。除Korec博士外，挪威专家Sundsbak博士和一名日本海军外科医生也在场诊治。经查，死者除因遭步枪枪托殴打造成的擦伤外，还有多处腹部伤口，据信系刺刀所致。其肠道穿孔，且失血过多，已处于垂危状态。

据悉，正在向涉事外国人及其他目击者采集证词，这些证词将在死因研讯中提交。从官方渠道获悉，英国当局将向日方提出抗议，但抗议的具体形式尚未披露。

pages.en:
Fine War Record
The late Mr. Tinkler was born
in Lancashire, England, in 1898, and
attended schools in that county
He enlisted with the British forces
during the war and was assigned
to the Royal Fusiliers, serving in
France with this unit, and was
awarded a Distinguished Conduct
Medal for meritorious service. Prior
to the completion of the World
War, he held the rank of corporal
and attended an Officers Training
School and while his appointment
for a commission was approved,
the armistice was signed before his
appointment as a commissioned
officer could take effect.
Mr. Tinkler came out to China
with the first appointees, which
numbered 40, for service with the
Shanghai Municipal Police, arriv-
ing here on August 10, 1919. He
served with the police department
in various capacities until his re-
signation on October 1, 1930.
Following his completion of ser-
vice with the S.M.C. police, he
visited the United States for six
months or more, and returned to
Shanghai following which he took
up a position with the China Print-
ing and Finishing Company, in the
capacity of labour superintendent
at the Company's Pootung Mills,
holding that position until the time
of his death. He was 41 years old.
The deceased was a bachelor and
had no relatives in Shanghai. He
was a well-built man enjoying good
physique and normal good health.
While on the police force he was
very popular with his colleagues and
associates, while officials of the
Pootung Mills state his services at
all times were of a very satisfac-
tory nature. In his younger days
he was an active participant in
athletic games, but never excep-
tionally outstanding.

Inquest Opened
The inquest on Mr. R. M. Tink-
ler, who died in the General
Hospital early yesterday morning
from wounds received in an en-
counter with Japanese marines in
Pootung, began yesterday morning
in the General Hospital. Mr. C. H.
Haines, H. M. Coroner, presided,
and formal identification of the
body took place.
Mr. Robert Cowan, a director of
the China Printing and Finishing
Company of 220 Szechuen Road,
gave evidence of identification of
the body of his former employee.
Mr. Cowan said that the deceased
was employed as the labour super-
intendent of the Company's cotton
mills in Pootung.
After the identification, the
coroner adjourned the inquest until
Wednesday, June 14 at 2.15 p.m.
pages.zh:
优异的战时履历
已故的丁克勒先生于1898年出生在英国兰开夏郡，并在该郡就读学校。战争期间他加入英军，被分配至皇家燧发枪团（Royal Fusiliers），随该部队在法国服役，并因功绩卓著被授予杰出行为勋章（Distinguished Conduct Medal）。在第一次世界大战结束前，他拥有下士军衔，并进入军官训练学校受训；虽然他的委任军官任命已获批准，但在其正式成为委任军官之前，停战协定便已签署。
丁克勒先生作为首批受聘于上海公共租界工部局警务处的40名人员之一来到中国，于1919年8月10日抵达此地。他在警务处担任各种职务，直至1930年10月1日辞职。
在完成工部局警务处的服务后，他访问美国六个月或更长时间，随后返回上海，之后在中国印染整理公司（China Printing and Finishing Company）任职，担任该公司浦东纱厂的劳工监工，一直担任该职直至去世。他享年41岁。
死者为单身，在上海无亲属。他体格健壮，身体素质良好，健康状况正常。在警队服役期间，他深受同事和伙伴的欢迎；而浦东纱厂的官员表示，他的服务始终令人非常满意。年轻时他曾积极参与体育比赛，但从未特别突出。

开启死因研讯
对R. M. 丁克勒先生的死因研讯于昨日上午在公济医院开始。丁克勒先生于昨日清晨在公济医院去世，死因是在浦东与日本海军陆战队发生冲突时受的伤。英国王室验尸官C. H. Haines先生主持了研讯，并对尸体进行了正式辨认。
四川路220号中国印染整理公司的董事Robert Cowan先生作证，辨认了其前雇员的尸体。Cowan先生说，死者受雇为该公司位于浦东的棉纺厂的劳工监工。
辨认结束后，验尸官宣布休庭，直至6月14日（星期三）下午2点15分继续研讯。

pages.en:
Tinkler Only
Wounded In
Mill Fracas

No Subsequent Injuries
Received By Deceased,
Says Navy Spokesman

VIOLET RESISTANCE
TO TREATMENT

Positively declaring that the
deceased had received no
further wounds after the fracas
which occurred in the pre-
mises of the Lun Chong Cotton
Mill, a Japanese naval spokes-
man threw some light yester-
day afternoon, at the press
conference, on the comparative
mystery which still shrouds the
death of Mr. R. M. Tinkler.
The spokesman admitted that Mr.
Tinkler had been struck on the head
with the rifle butt by a sailor, and
in the ensuing scuffle the deceased
"may have come into contact with
the bayonets of the Japanese Naval
Landing Part units on the scene."
It was also definitely established
that the blow on the head was the
first injury suffered by the deceased.
The Japanese voiced the belief
yesterday, through the medium of
a statement by the Japanese naval
surgeon who attended Mr. Tinkler
at the General Hospital on Tuesday
evening, that had not the deceased
resisted all efforts to dress his
wounds, he might never have suc-
cumbed to his injuries.

Case Not Closed

In reply to a question as to whe-
ther the case was closed from the
Japanese point of view, the spokes-
man declared that future "demands"
would be presented to the British
authorities, but that no other pro-
tests, except those handed to the
British Consul-General by Mr.
Miura on Tuesday afternoon, were
in immediate contemplation.
From answers given by the
spokesman yesterday evening to the
barrage of questions shot at him
from all sides it appears that Mr.
Tinkler, following the scuffle at the
mill, was taken to the Naval Land-
ing Party headquarters, in Pootung,
being carried part of the way and—
at his own request—walking the re-
mainder of the distance unaided.
Arriving at Headquarters, he was
taken to the infirmary and his
wounds were given immediate at-
tention. Mr. Tinkler was in a de-
lirious mood, the spokesman said,
and kept falling off his bed, finally
being placed on a Japanese mat on
the floor.
pages.zh:
仅丁克勒一人在
工厂冲突中受伤

死者未受后续伤害，
海军发言人称

顽强抗拒治疗

一位日本海军发言人昨日下午在新闻发布会上，就仍笼罩着R. M. 丁克勒先生死亡之谜的部分情况提供了一些线索，他明确宣称，死者在伦昌棉纺厂 premises 内发生的冲突之后未再受到其他伤害。
该发言人承认，丁克勒先生曾被一名水兵用步枪枪托击中头部，在随后的扭打中，死者“可能接触到了现场日本海军陆战队单位的刺刀”。此外还确切证实，头部受击是死者遭受的第一处伤害。
昨日，通过周二晚间在公济医院诊治丁克勒先生的日本海军外科医生的声明，日方表达了一种看法：如果死者没有抗拒所有包扎伤口的努力，他或许不会因伤致死。

案件未结

当被问及从日方角度看案件是否已结案时，该发言人宣称，未来将向英国当局提出“要求”，但除了三浦（Miura）先生于周二下午递交给英国总领事的抗议外，目前没有其他立即考虑的抗议行动。
从该发言人昨晚对各方连珠炮般提问的回答来看，丁克勒先生在工厂扭打后，被带往浦东的海军陆战队总部，部分路程由人搀扶或抬送，其余路程则应其本人要求自行行走。到达总部后，他被送往医务室，伤口立即得到处理。发言人称，丁克勒先生当时处于谵妄状态，不断从床上跌落，最后被安置在地板上的日式席子上。

pages.en:
Resisted All Advances
He resisted all advances on the
part of the Japanese to treat his
wounds, flaying his arms about for
several hours when approached.
Only when his condition appeared
to have taken a turn for the worse
was it deemed necessary by the
Japanese to remove him to the
General Hospital.
Answering another question, the
spokesman emphasized that there
was no record of Mr. Tinkler having
demanded the attendance of his own
doctor at the General Hospital, add-
ing that shortly before his death he
was asked—in the presence of wit-
nesses—whether he had anything to
say, but replied in the negative,
merely thanking the surgeon for his
efforts.
The reason for his detention by
the Japanese authorities until his
death, the spokesman said, was for
the purpose of pursuing investiga-
tions of the incident.
The spokesman denied knowledge
of when Mr. Tinkler's wounds were
first treated, or the report that two
Japanese sentries had been placed
on guard outside the operating
theatre at the General Hospital.
The men who wielded the bayonets
that wounded Mr. Tinkler were also
unknown to the spokesman.
pages.zh:
抗拒一切救治尝试
他抗拒日方对其伤口进行的一切处理尝试，当有人靠近时，他挥舞双臂持续了数小时。只有当他的状况似乎恶化时，日方才认为有必要将他送往公济医院。
在回答另一个问题时，该发言人强调，没有记录显示丁克勒先生要求在公济医院由其自己的医生诊治，并补充说，在他临终前不久，有人在见证人在场的情况下询问他是否有话要说，但他予以否定，仅感谢了外科医生的努力。
发言人称，日本当局将其扣留直至死亡的原因，是为了对该事件进行调查。
该发言人否认知晓丁克勒先生的伤口首次得到治疗的时间，也否认有关两名日本哨兵被部署在公济医院手术室外站岗的报道。对于用刺刀刺伤丁克勒先生的人员，该发言人也表示不知情。

pages.en:
LONDON IS TAKING
SERIOUS VIEW

Allegation Of Nipponese
Fomenting Trouble In
Mill District

LONDON, June 7.—The British
Government is taking an extremely
serious view of the incident in the
Pootung on June 6, in which a
British employee of a British firm,
the China Printing and Finishing
Company, and Japanese bluejackets
were involved, as a sequel of which,
the British subject, R. M. Tinkler,
lost his life.
It is pointed out that the Japan-
ese are virtually in control of the
mill area and that for some time,
there have been disturbances among
the workers.
Following British protests, an
armed British naval guard was
mounted over the mill but was
withdrawn after a few days on the
receipt of a written assurance from
the Japanese that British lives and
property would be protected.
Only yesterday, Sir Robert Crai-
gie, the British Ambassador in
Tokyo, raised the matter with the
Ministry of Foreign Affairs, drawing
attention to the activities of certain
Japanese in fomenting the strikers,
and the absence of steps by the
Japanese to preserve law and order.
—Reuter.

Tokyo Version
TOKYO, June 7.—The Japanese
Foreign Office spokesman's version
of the incident in Pootung yester-
day, in which a British subject, R.
M. Tinkler was involved, states:
"A fight broke out between 400
non-strikers and strikers. When
Japanese Marines were about to
take the ring-leaders to their head-
quarters, the Briton suddenly ap-
peared and fired on them."—Reuter.
pages.zh:
伦敦方面严肃看待

指控日本人煽动
工厂区麻烦

伦敦，6月7日电——英国政府极为严肃地看待6月6日发生在浦东的事件，该事件涉及一家英国公司——中国印染整理公司的英国雇员和日本水兵，作为后续结果，英国臣民R. M. 丁克勒丧生。
有人指出，日本人实际上控制着工厂区域，且一段时间以来，工人中间一直存在骚乱。
在英国提出抗议后，一支武装英国海军警卫队被部署在工厂上方，但在收到日方关于保护英国人生命和财产的书面保证后，几天后便撤走了。
就在昨天，英国驻东京大使罗伯特·克雷吉爵士（Sir Robert Craigie）向外交部提出了此事，提请注意某些日本人在煽动罢工者方面的活动，以及日方在维护法律和秩序方面缺乏举措。——路透社。

东京版本
东京，6月7日电——日本外务省发言人昨日就涉及英国臣民R. M. 丁克勒的浦东事件发表的版本称：“400名非罢工者与罢工者之间爆发了战斗。当日本海军陆战队正准备将头目带往其总部时，这名英国人突然出现并向他们开枪。”——路透社。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
JUN 8 1939

Strong Japanese Reactions
To Pootung Incident

Consulate-General Spokesman Says Action Of Late
Mr. Tinkler Was One Of Lawlessness And
Gravity; Manhandling Justified

Actions of the late R. M. Tink-
ler, 41-year-old employee of the
China Printing and Finishing Com-
pany at the firm's Pootung Point
works on Tuesday morning, con-
stituted "a deliberate insult" to the
Japanese Navy, Mr. Ken Tsurumi,
spokesman for the Japanese Con-
sulate-General in Shanghai, said
yesterday.
"This is not an issue involving
the pointing of a gun by a Briton
towards a Japanese," he said. "It
involves an act of lawlessness to-
wards officers in uniform. Hence
its extreme gravity."
Mr. Tsurumi expressed surprise
that Tinkler had "not been shot
and killed on the spot."
The spokesman recalled that the
Japanese Naval Landing Party had
stationed a force at the mill on May
24 following a request by the Bri-
tish Consulate-General for measures
to protect the property in view of
the prevailing strike.
"Yesterday, he continued," when
a dispute arose between strikers
and non-strikers, the Japanese
Naval Landing Party did its best
to suppress the disturbance.

Arrogant Attitude
"At this time, trouble arose be-
tween the British employees of the
plant and the landing party. One
Briton from this group, displaying
an extremely arrogant attitude,
went about pointing a gun at Ja-
panese section, company and batta-
lion commanders. He even fired a
shot.
"This was a grave provocation
towards the Japanese Navy. It is
not difficult to imagine the indigna-
tion his actions gave rise to among
the men who saw their superior
officers being insulted.
"That they should have disarmed
this dangerous character in self-
defence and that they should have
subsequently manhandled him is
only natural under the circum-
stances," the consular spokesman
declared.

"Makeshift" Solution Rejected
An "indefinite and makeshift"
settlement of the Anglo-Japanese
incident at the China Printing and
Finishing Company's Pootung Point
plant in which R. M. Tinkler was
alleged to have fired a pistol at a
Japanese bluejacket and subse-
quently threatened Japanese offi-
cers with his weapon "cannot be
tolerated," the "Tairiku Shimpo,"
local Japanese daily, declared in an
editorial yesterday. "The firing
of a gun at the Japanese military
within Japanese occupied territory
is a case of unprecedented gravity,"
the newspaper said.
The Japanese authorities were
urged by the journal to face the
issue "with a firm determination,
so that the indignation caused by
the affair among the local Japan-
ese residents shall not be in vain."
"The Britons who caused the
present incident may be hoodlums
hired by the company as strike
breakers. But that is not the point.
They may be uneducated hoodlums
but their impertinence and viol-
ence represents the contempt and
enmity of Britons as a whole to-
wards Japan," the journal declar-
ed.

"Deliberate Provocation"
The case, the newspaper declar-
ed, "is gaining gravity as a deliber-
ate insult and provocation of the
British towards the Japanese armed
forces."
"As the Japanese Naval Landing
Party, in keeping with its previous
assurances, moved to curb violence
by the strikers, employees of the
firm returned kindness with insults
and threats instead of gratitude.
Moreover, using a firearm which
should not have been there, an
attempt was made by an employee
to shoot a Japanese bluejacket.
This was not a mistake, but a in-
sult and a provocation. It should
be treated by the Japanese auth-
orities as a challenge," the news-
paper declared.
The firm management, the "Tai-
riku Shimpo" declared, had ex-
pressed its regrets and apologies,
while Sir Herbert Phillips, the
British Consul-General, had ex-
pressed his regrets that the incid-
ent should have occurred when a
protest was lodged by Japanese
Consul-General Yoshiaki Miura, on
Tuesday.
"But as stated before this was
not an accident or a mistake.
Should this case be settled as in
the past with a mere apology and
assurance against a future repeti-
tion it is to be feared that a grave
source of danger for the future
will be left," the newspaper de-
clared.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年6月8日

日本对浦东事件反应强烈

总领事馆发言人称已故丁克勒先生的行为属无法无天且性质严重；殴打行为具有正当性

上海日本总领事馆发言人鹤见健（Ken Tsurumi）先生昨日表示，周二上午，在中国印刷整理公司（China Printing and Finishing Company）位于浦东角（Pootung Point）的工厂内，该公司41岁的雇员R. M. 丁克勒（R. M. Tinkler）先生的行为构成了对日本海军的“蓄意侮辱”。

他说：“这并非英国人用枪指着日本人的问题。这是针对身穿制服的军官实施的无法无天的行为。因此其性质极其严重。”

鹤见先生对丁克勒未被“当场击毙”表示惊讶。

该发言人回顾称，鉴于当时罢工盛行，应英国总领事馆关于保护财产的要求，日本海军陆战队已于5月24日在该纱厂部署了兵力。

他继续说道：“昨天，当罢工者与非罢工者之间发生争执时，日本海军陆战队尽力平息骚乱。”

傲慢态度

“此时，工厂的英国雇员与陆战队之间发生了冲突。这群人中有一名英国人表现出极其傲慢的态度，四处用枪指着日本分队长、连长和营长。他甚至开了一枪。

“这是对日本海军的严重挑衅。不难想象，目睹上级军官受辱的士兵们心中激起了怎样的愤怒。

“在这种情况下，他们解除这个危险人物的武装并随后对其施以殴打，是再自然不过的事情，”该领事馆发言人宣称。

拒绝“临时”解决方案

当地日文日报《大陆新报》昨日在一篇社论中宣称，对于中国印刷整理公司浦东角工厂发生的英日事件，即据称R. M. 丁克勒向一名日本水兵开枪并随后用武器威胁日本军官一事，任何“不确定且临时凑合”的解决方案都“不能容忍”。该报称：“在日本占领区内向日本军队开枪，是前所未有的严重事件。”

该报敦促日本当局“以坚定的决心”面对这一问题，“以免当地日本居民因此事产生的愤慨落空”。

该报宣称：“引发当前事件的英国人可能是公司雇佣来破坏罢工的流氓。但这不是重点。他们可能是未受过教育的流氓，但他们的无礼和暴力代表了全体英国人对日本的蔑视和敌意。”

“蓄意挑衅”

该报宣称，此案“作为英国人对日本武装部队的蓄意侮辱和挑衅，性质正日益严重”。

“当日本海军陆战队按照此前的保证，采取行动遏制罢工者的暴力行为时，该公司员工非但没有感激，反而以侮辱和威胁作为回报。此外，一名员工企图使用本不该出现的枪支射击一名日本水兵。这不是失误，而是侮辱和挑衅。日本当局应将其视为一种挑战，”该报宣称。

《大陆新报》宣称，公司管理层已表示遗憾和道歉，而英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）在周二日本总领事三浦义明（Yoshiaki Miura）提出抗议时，也对发生此类事件表示了遗憾。

“但如前所述，这并非意外或失误。如果此案像过去那样仅以道歉和保证不再重演来了结，恐怕会为未来留下严重的危险根源，”该报宣称。

pages.en:
Crowd Expected At
Deceased's Funeral
To-morrow At 2.30

A large gathering is expect-
ed at the funeral of the late
Mr. R. M. Tinkler to-morrow
afternoon when many of the
deceased's former colleagues in
the Shanghai Municipal Police
and others will attend. Funeral
arrangements are in the hands
of the International Funeral
Directors and interment will
take place in the Hungjao
Cemetery at 2.30 p.m. The
Very Rev. Dean Trivett will
officiate at the graveside.
pages.zh:
预计明日午后二时半
死者葬礼将有大群民众出席

预计明天下午参加已故R. M. 丁克勒先生葬礼的人将很多，死者在上海公共租界工部局警务处的许多前同事及其他人士将出席。葬礼事宜由国际殡仪馆（International Funeral Directors）承办，下午2时30分在虹桥公墓（Hungjao Cemetery）下葬。特里维特主任牧师（The Very Rev. Dean Trivett）将在墓前主持仪式。

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.
JUN 8 1939

The Tinkler Incident

THE incidents involving Japan and Britain which have occurred during the last few days have been climaxed most unfortunately by the death of Mr. R. M. Tinkler, who has succumbed to bayonet wounds received during a scuffle with Japanese Naval Landing Party details in Pootung.

It is quite plain that Mr. Tinkler's death as well as the train of events leading up to his detention cannot at the present time be viewed as an isolated incident involving only the victim or his employers, the China Printing and Finishing Company. Instead, it evidently has a much wider and important implication in view of the detention of two British military officers in North China and the "ultimatum" presented by the Japanese to the British Concession authorities in Tientsin.

In examining the events which culminated with the death of Mr. Tinkler, one must be forced to rely on the limited amount of information which is available at the time of writing. It is alleged that Mr. Tinkler, who was a member of the personnel staff of the strike-ridden Lun Chong mill, threatened the Japanese bluejackets and officers with a gun and that one shot was fired during the scuffle, although no information from neutral sources is yet available to substantiate either of the charges contained in the Japanese report.

During the altercation, Mr. Tinkler was said to have been hit on the head with a rifle butt by a Japanese sailor, but the wound, according to Japanese reports available on the night of the incident, was not indicated as being of a serious nature. Mr. Tinkler, according to the Japanese, was able to walk to the headquarters of the Naval Landing Party.

No mention was made of the fact that Mr. Tinkler had been bayonetted, but it is quite clear that no medical attention was given to the victim from the time of the assault until he was brought to the General Hospital in a dying condition after 11 o'clock at night. On this particular point, there seems no need for any comment for there is every indication of neglect in saving the life of the victim in so far as giving him prompt medical aid was concerned.

Mr. Tinkler's death, as we pointed out in the beginning, assumes far greater significance when one considers the events in connection with the detention of the two British military officers in Kalgan. Both Lieutenant-Colonel C. R. Spear and Lieutenant Cooper, according to reports available here, were carrying identifying credentials and were traveling as accredited representatives of the British Government. It is difficult indeed to find any reasonable grounds whereby one could accept the Japanese view that both men are "common spies" and that they deserve to be treated as such.

The incident involving Mr. Tinkler, the detention of the two British officers as well as the "ultimatum" presented by the Japanese authorities to the Tientsin British Concession authorities all tend to indicate that there exists a desire on the part of the Japanese to intimidate Britons in China.

This is indeed the only possible way to interpret the events of the past week. During the past few months there has been a violent anti-British campaign in the Japanese-controlled papers in China and these have been followed by the present series of incidents which by an unexplainable coincidence involved nationals of no other power but Britain.

Significant is the fact that while these "pin prick" tactics are being used against Britain, the Japanese are trying by every means to refrain from antagonizing the United States. It will be recalled that the Japanese representations to the American authorities on the alleged misuse of foreign flags were considerably more moderate in tone than a similar protest to Britain.

This discrimination in favor of the United States shows quite plainly that there is a desire to split the so-called "united front" of the foreign powers in China. Britain, France and the United States are by no means unaware of such a policy on the part of Tokyo and it is also quite evident that they are prepared to stick together for their common interest regardless of the favor and disfavor manifested by the Japanese toward their own individual interests. In the Kulangsu incident there is a clear proof of the readiness and determination of the three powers to take joint action to protect their common interests.

The incidents leading up to the attack on Mr. Tinkler and the arrest of the two British officers involve, therefore, not the safety of only Britons residing and traveling in China. Upon the outcome of these incidents and the way they are handled by the British Government, with the support of the other powers, must rest today the safety of all foreigners residing and traveling in Japanese-controlled territory regardless of their nationality. It is in this respect that all foreign powers having treaty relations with China have an interest in the death of Mr. Tinkler and the incidents in North China.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》。
1939年6月8日

丁克勒事件

近日发生的涉及日本和英国的事件，不幸以R. M. 丁克勒先生的死亡达到高潮，他在浦东与日本海军陆战队分遣队发生扭打时身受刺刀伤，不治身亡。

很明显，丁克勒先生的死亡以及导致他被拘留的一系列事件，目前不能被视为仅涉及受害者或其雇主中国印刷整理公司的孤立事件。相反，鉴于两名英国军官在华北被拘留，以及日本向天津英国租界当局提出的“最后通牒”，此事显然具有更广泛和重要的意义。

在审视以丁克勒先生死亡为结局的事件时，人们不得不依赖写作时可获得的有限信息。据称，身为深受罢工困扰的伦钟纱厂（Lun Chong mill，音译）人事部门成员的丁克勒先生，曾用枪威胁日本水兵和军官，且在扭打期间开了一枪，尽管目前尚无来自中立方面的信息来证实日本报告中所载的任何一项指控。

据说在争吵过程中，丁克勒先生被一名日本水手用枪托击中头部，但根据事发当晚可获得的日本报告，该伤口并未显示为严重性质。据日方称，丁克勒先生能够步行至海军陆战队总部。

报告中未提及丁克勒先生被刺刀刺伤的事实，但很明显，从遭受袭击到深夜11点后被送往总医院时已处于垂危状态期间，受害者未得到任何医疗救治。在这一特定问题上，似乎无需多言，因为在给予及时医疗救助以挽救受害者生命方面，存在明显的疏忽迹象。

正如我们在开头指出的那样，考虑到与两名英国军官在张家口（Kalgan）被拘留有关的事件，丁克勒先生的死亡具有更为重大的意义。根据此处可获得的报告，C. R. 斯皮尔中校（Lieutenant-Colonel C. R. Spear）和库珀中尉（Lieutenant Cooper）均携带身份证明文件，并作为英国政府的认证代表出行。确实很难找到任何合理的理由来接受日方的观点，即这两人都是“普通间谍”并应受到如此对待。

涉及丁克勒先生的事件、两名英国军官的被拘留，以及日本当局向天津英国租界当局提出的“最后通牒”，都倾向于表明日本方面有意恐吓在华英国人。

这确实是解释过去一周事件的唯一可能方式。在过去几个月里，日本在华控制的报纸上开展了激烈的反英运动，随之而来的是目前这一系列事件，这些事件以一种无法解释的巧合，涉及的仅是英国国民，而无其他强国国民。

值得注意的是，在对英国使用这些“零星骚扰”战术的同时，日本正试图通过各种手段避免激怒美国。回想起来，日本当局就所谓滥用外国旗帜一事向美国当局提出的交涉，其语气比向英国提出的类似抗议要温和得多。

这种偏向美国的歧视清楚地表明，日本有意分裂所谓在华外国列强的“统一战线”。英国、法国和美国绝非不知道东京方面的这种政策，而且很明显，无论日本对其各自利益表现出 favor 还是 disfavor，他们都准备为了共同利益团结一致。在鼓浪屿事件中，清楚地证明了这三个强国采取联合行动保护其共同利益的意愿和决心。

因此，导致袭击丁克勒先生和逮捕两名英国军官的事件，涉及的不仅仅是在华居住和旅行的英国人的安全。所有这些居住在 Japanese-controlled territory（日本控制区）并在此旅行的外国人，无论其国籍如何，今日的安全都取决于这些事件的结果以及英国政府在其他列强支持下处理这些事件的方式。正是在这方面，所有与中国有条约关系的外国列强都对丁克勒先生的死亡和华北事件利害攸关。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

JUN 8 1939

THE POOTUNG AFFAIR

Correspondents who have written expressing their views on the subject of the incident at Pootung which resulted in the death yesterday morning of Mr. R. M. Tinkler are informed that their communications cannot be printed at the moment. With the opening of the inquest yesterday morning the whole matter has now become sub judice and it would be contempt of court to make any comment upon it. It would be as well, however, to remember that the account of the affair which appeared in the local Press yesterday morning was a purely ex parte statement by the Japanese officials, and in this connection it may be remembered that one tale is good until another is told. There are, in the statement made by the Japanese spokesman, many matters which will undoubtedly be elucidated in the course of the inquiry which has been commenced by the British authorities, not the least important of which is the omission on the part of the spokesman to make any reference to what happened to Mr. Tinkler save to state that he was hit with the butt end of a rifle by a Japanese sailor. Nothing was said of the stab wounds which it is now alleged were inflicted upon the dead man, nor when they were administered. When the inquest has been completed and the true facts of the case ascertained it will be possible properly to comment on what appears, even on the statements of the Japanese spokesman, and upon what he apparently omitted to say, a very grave matter indeed.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年6月8日

浦东事件

那些写信表达对浦东事件看法的通讯员获悉，他们的来信目前无法刊登。随着昨天上午验尸审讯的开始，整个案件现在已成为 sub judice（待决案件），对此发表评论将构成藐视法庭。然而，最好记住的是，昨天早上当地报纸上刊登的关于该事件的报道纯粹是日本官员的单方面陈述，在这方面，不妨记住“一面之词不足为信，兼听则明”。在日本发言人的声明中，有许多事项无疑将在英国当局开始的调查过程中得到澄清，其中最重要的是，发言人除了 stating that he was hit with the butt end of a rifle by a Japanese sailor（陈述他被一名日本水手用枪托击中）之外，只字未提丁克勒先生遭遇了什么。对于现在据称施加在死者身上的刺伤，只字未提，也未说明是何时造成的。当验尸审讯完成并查明案件真实情况后，才有可能对即使根据日本发言人的陈述也显得非常严重的事情，以及他显然遗漏未说的内容，进行适当的评论。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES,

JUN 8 1939

Extrality
Rights May
Be Limited

Japanese Reserve Right
To Take What Steps
They See Fit

“If an individual, having extra-
territorial rights, threatens the
safety of Japanese forces in Japan-
ese-occupied territory, his extra-
territorial rights may be limited,”
declared the Japanese Embassy
spokesman yesterday afternoon in
answer to a question regarding the
legal status of a foreigner who resist-
ed Japanese forces in the execution
of their duty.
As a matter of principle, the
spokesman continued, the Japanese
intend to recognise these privileges
wherever possible, but reserve the
right—to which they are entitled
by International law—to deal with
any person endangering the safety
of the Japanese forces as they see
fit.
It is not a question, he declared,
of application of the law, but of
direct, of summary, action to pro-
tect the safety of the Japanese
forces involved.

Individual Action
Asked to define the words “sum-
mary action,” the spokesman said
that individual steps would be taken
in each case. In answer to the
question: “Could the term summary
action be applied to the Tinkler
case?” the spokesman replied in
the affirmative.
The remedy that the Japanese
would adopt, however, he added,
would be only in the event of ex-
treme necessity, dependent on the
gravity of the case in hand.
Extraterritorial rights, the spokes-
man also stated, involved only
China and not Japan, but the
Japanese authorities, nevertheless,
intended to respect and recognize
these privileges.
“Japanese forces in occupation in
China,” he concluded, “have wrested
Chinese sovereignty from these
areas for the purpose of military
operations, but if anyone should
conflict with Chinese law in these
areas he would be dealt with as
previously, provided the infraction
does not impede the progress of
Japanese operations.”
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，

1939年6月8日

治外法权
权利或受
限制

日本保留采取
其认为适当之
措施的权利

“若拥有治外法权之个人，在日军占领区威胁到日军部队之安全，其治外法权可受限制，”日本大使馆发言人昨日下午在回答关于外国人抵抗日军执行职务时之法律地位的问题时宣称。

发言人继续称，原则上，日本打算在可能范围内承认这些特权，但保留根据国际法所赋予的权利，即按其认为适当的方式处理任何危及日军安全之人。

他宣称，这并非适用法律的问题，而是为保护所涉日军部队之安全而采取的直接的、即决的行动。

个别行动

当被要求界定“即决行动”一词的含义时，发言人表示，将在每个案件中采取个别步骤。针对“即决行动一词是否适用于丁克勒（Tinkler）案？”这一问题，发言人给予了肯定答复。

但他补充说，日本将采取的补救措施仅在极端必要的情况下实施，取决于手头案件的严重程度。

发言人还指出，治外法权仅涉及中国而不涉及日本，但日本当局仍打算尊重并承认这些特权。

他总结道：“在中国占领区的日军部队，出于军事行动之目的，已从这些区域夺取了中国主权，但若有人在这些区域违反中国法律，只要该违法行为不妨碍日军行动的进展，仍将按以往方式处理。”

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.
14311
6968
JUN 9 1939

British Consul Protests Acts
Of Japanese In Pootung Area

Fosterage Of Anti-British Propaganda Cause Of
Formal Representations; Remedy Requested

Direct verbal representations against Japanese fosterage of anti-British agitation in Pootung were made to Japanese Consul-General Yoshiaki Miura by Sir Herbert Phillips, British Consul-General, yesterday morning, according to information received by THE CHINA PRESS last night.

The report revealed that the British official called upon Mr. Miura a little more than an hour before the start of the consular reception yesterday morning on the occasion of the King's Birthday, at which Sir Herbert was host.

The endorsement by Japanese armed forces of anti-British labor agitation, and the interference by armed Japanese plainclothes men early yesterday morning with British-employed Chinese labor were said to have been brought up in the course of the verbal representations.

Asks Prevention

Sir Herbert is said to have requested Mr. Miura to take such steps as would be necessary for the prevention of a recurrence of such activity by Japanese.

The British official was stated to have referred to an incident which occurred at the Lun Chong printing plant at the Pai Lien Ching Creek in Pootung, close to the Robert Dollar Wharf, not to be confused with the Lun Chong Cotton Mill at Pootung Point where the Tinkler incident occurred Tuesday morning.

The British consul-general stated that armed Japanese plainclothes men had prevented laborers from returning to the British-owned printing plant to work, despite the fact that the strike has already been settled.

Earlier reports yesterday stated that the plainclothes men opened fire in their efforts to prevent the laborers from resuming work, and that a Chinese bystander was wounded and taken to a hospital in Nantao.

"No Firing"

No mention of Sir Herbert's call upon Mr. Miura was made at the Japanese press conference last night. The navy spokesman, however, stated that there had been no firing at the Lun Chong printing plant. "The Japanese authorities are taking extensive precautions to maintain peace and order there," he told newsmen.

The spokesman had "no information" with regard to anti-British demonstrations in Pootung in which Japanese soldiers took part yesterday morning.

Asked whether there had been any demonstrations of this nature at all in recent weeks, he stated that "there may have been by strikers." He had "no information" as to this also.

When asked whether the Japanese authorities had done anything to prevent a demonstration by strikers, he replied, "As stated before, the Japanese forces are not there to intervene between capital and labor. They are there just to maintain peace and order."

Lile
R 9/6
C 9/6

《大美晚报》。
14311
6968
1939年6月9日

英国领事抗议日本
在浦东地区之行为

纵容反英宣传系正式交涉之起因；要求予以补救

据《大美晚报》昨晚收到的消息，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）于昨日上午向日本总领事三浦义明（Yoshiaki Miura）就日本纵容浦东地区反英煽动一事进行了直接口头交涉。

报道披露，这位英国官员是在昨日上午国王诞辰领事招待会开始前一个多小时拜访三浦先生的，该招待会由赫伯特爵士主持。

据说，在口头交涉过程中，提到了日本武装部队支持反英劳工骚乱，以及武装日本便衣人员于昨日清晨干涉受雇于英国人的中国劳工之事。

要求防止

据说赫伯特爵士要求三浦先生采取必要步骤，以防止日本人此类活动再次发生。

据称，这位英国官员提及了一起发生在浦东白莲泾（Pai Lien Ching Creek）、靠近罗伯特·多尔码头（Robert Dollar Wharf）的伦昌印刷厂（Lun Chong printing plant）的事件，请勿将其与周二上午发生丁克勒事件的位于浦东角的伦昌棉纺厂（Lun Chong Cotton Mill）混淆。

英国总领事称，尽管罢工已经解决，但武装日本便衣人员仍阻止劳工返回这家英资印刷厂工作。

昨日较早的报道称，便衣人员为阻止劳工复工而开枪，一名中国旁观者受伤并被送往南市的一家医院。

“未开枪”

在日本昨晚的新闻发布会上，未提及赫伯特爵士拜访三浦先生一事。然而，海军发言人表示，在伦昌印刷厂并未发生开枪事件。“日本当局正在那里采取广泛预防措施以维持和平与秩序，”他告诉记者。

对于昨日早晨有日本士兵参与的反英示威活动，发言人表示“没有信息”。

当被问及最近几周是否发生过此类示威活动时，他表示“罢工者可能有过”。对此他也表示“没有信息”。

当被问及日本当局是否采取了任何措施来防止罢工者的示威活动时，他回答说：“如前所述，日军并非介入资方与劳方之间。他们在那里只是为了维持和平与秩序。”

Lile
R 9/6
C 9/6

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
JUN 9 1939
14316
British Will Lodge Protest
Over Tinkler Killing
Strong Note Will Be Sent in Connection
With Bayonetting of Briton in Pootung
A VERY strong protest will be lodged by the British Consular authori-
ties with Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-General in Shanghai, in
connection with the death on Wednesday morning of Mr. Richard
Maurice Tinkler as the result of wounds received during a fight with
Japanese sailors at Pootung premises of the China Printing & Finishing
Co.'s Lun Chong mill, where he was employed as labour superintendent,
on Tuesday morning, the "North-China Daily News" was informed
last night by a British Consular official. In connection with the situa-
tion at the mill and in Pootung where anti-British demonstrations are
prevalent and where China Printing & Finishing Co. employees have
been threatened by armed bands, strong representations were made to
the Japanese authorities yesterday, he stated, but no protests had been
entered yet in connection with Mr. Tinkler's death.
In connection with Mr. Tinkler's
death the Japanese naval spokesman
at yesterday's conference stated that
certain persons believed that the
man was stabbed after his removal to
the Japanese company headquarters
and that therefore he wished to
make the following facts known:
"When Tinkler pointed a Mauser
pistol at an officer standing in front
of him," the spokesman stated, "a
Petty Officer standing on his right,
hit Tinkler's fore-arm with his rifle
butt causing the former to drop his
gun. Tinkler thereupon proceeded
to grapple with the petty officer,
knocking him down from behind.
Seeing this, the section commander
who was at the scene at the time,
hit Tinkler with the scabbard of his
sword but at the same time the man
held by Tinkler, shook off the latter,
by hitting him in the leg with his
rifle. Other sailors then surrounded
the scene with bayonets fixed to
their rifles but the petty-officer gave
orders that Tinkler should not be
bayonetted, which order was heard
by all the sailors in the group.
Tinkler continued to fight, however,
and a general scuffle ensued, during
which one sailor remembers that
Tinkler came into contact with his
bayonet."
Lying on Back
"Apparently," the spokesman con-
tinued, "Tinkler came into contact
with the bayonet during this scuffle
and when the fight was over, he
lay on the ground with arms out-
stretched, still conscious and still
desirous of fighting. A number of
sailors were then ordered to pick him
up by his arms and legs, but after
having carried him for about 10
metres, Tinkler said that he prefer-
red to walk. It was whilst he was
being carried that those in the group
first saw that he was bleeding from
the abdomen."
"At the time," the spokesman con-
tinue, "three British employees of the
China Printing and Finishing Co.,
among them Messrs. H. Stott and J.
Sharples, asked for permission to
accompany Tinkler to the Japanese
headquarters, which permission was
granted. As soon as the group ar-
rived at the Japanese headquarters,
Tinkler was taken to the infirmary.
This was at 9.40 a.m. Japan time
(i.e. 8.40 a.m. Shanghai time). The
attending surgeon told Tinkler to
undress and to lie down on the
operating table, but he refused to
do so. The Britishers who had ac-
companied him, assisted by a Japan-
ese male nurse, then ripped off his
clothing, but he kept moving about
whilst the same male nurse, assisted
by Tinkler's friends, held him down
so as to permit first-aid to be ad-
ministered. It was found that he
had an injury on the abdomen, but
he moved too much to enable the
surgeon to ascertain the extent and
seriousness of the wound.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，
1939年6月9日
14316
英国将就丁克勒遇害
提出抗议
将就英人在浦东被刺刀刺伤一事
发出强硬照会
据一位英国领事官员昨晚告知《字林西报》，英国领事当局将就理查德·莫里斯·丁克勒（Richard Maurice Tinkler）先生之死，向日本驻上海总领事三浦义明（Y. Miura）先生提出非常强烈的抗议。丁克勒受雇于中国印染整理公司（China Printing & Finishing Co.）伦昌工厂担任劳工主管，于周二上午在该厂浦东厂区与日本水兵发生打斗期间受伤，并于周三上午身亡。该官员称，鉴于该工厂及浦东地区的局势——当地反英示威盛行，且中国印染整理公司员工受到武装团伙威胁——昨日已向日本当局提出了强烈交涉，但尚未就丁克勒先生之死提出抗议。

关于丁克勒先生之死，日本海军发言人在昨天的记者会上表示，有些人认为该男子在被移送至日本公司总部后遭到刺伤，因此他希望公布以下事实：

发言人称：“当丁克勒用一把毛瑟手枪指着他面前的一名军官时，站在他右侧的一名士官用枪托击打丁克勒的前臂，导致前者丢掉了枪。丁克勒随即与该名士官扭打，从背后将其击倒。当时在场的分队长见状，用剑鞘击打丁克勒，但与此同时，被丁克勒抓住的人用步枪击打丁克勒的腿部，从而挣脱了后者。随后其他水兵围住现场，步枪上已装上刺刀，但士官下令不得用刺刀刺丁克勒，周围所有水兵都听到了这道命令。然而，丁克勒继续搏斗，随之发生了一场混战，期间一名水兵记得丁克勒碰到了他的刺刀。”

仰面躺着

发言人继续说道：“显然，丁克勒在这场混战中碰到了刺刀，打斗结束后，他躺在地上，双臂伸展，仍有意识且仍想战斗。随后几名水兵奉命抓住他的手臂和腿将他抬起，但在抬了大约10米后，丁克勒表示他更愿意自己走。正是在他被抬着的时候，人群中的人第一次看到他腹部在流血。”

发言人接着说：“当时，中国印染整理公司的三名英国雇员，包括H. Stott先生和J. Sharples先生，请求允许陪同丁克勒前往日本总部，该请求获准。一行人抵达日本总部后，丁克勒立即被送往医务室。此时是日本时间上午9点40分（即上海时间上午8点40分）。主治医生让丁克勒脱衣并躺在手术台上，但他拒绝这样做。陪同他的英国人在一名日本男护士的协助下撕开了他的衣服，但他不停挣扎，而同名男护士在丁克勒朋友的协助下按住他，以便进行急救。发现他腹部有伤，但他动作太大，医生无法确定伤口的范围和严重程度。”

pages.en:
All the other wounds were treated,
however, this taking about one hour
and not three, as I had mentioned
yesterday. Tinkler was then taken to
a ward where he was requested to
lie down. He complained about his
pillow being too low, and another one
was given him. Two of the Britons
then left at short intervals, but the
third remained until 3 p.m. (Shang-
hai time) when he was told that his
staying could not serve any useful
purpose, whereupon he too, returned
to the mill."

Friends Summoned

"Tinkler was asked whether he
wanted anything," the spokesman
continued, "and he was given a glass
of water for which he had asked.
The water which was given him was
brought from Japan because Shanghai
water is not pure enough. The in-
jured man was then given an injec-
tion of morphine and at noon he was
asked whether he wanted to eat but
he said that he was not hungry. As
long as Tinkler was in Pootung, a
surgeon and a male nurse remained in
an adjoining room. At 5.30 p.m.
(Japan time), he was found perspiring
and spitting blood, whereupon the
surgeon drew the conclusion that he
was suffering from an internal
haemorrhage. No improvement being
noticeable at 8 p.m. (Shanghai time)
Naval Landing Party Headquarters
were advised, whilst Tinkler was
given a camphor injection and two
Japanese female attendants were
secured to look after him. Asked
whether he wanted anything, he said
that he would like to see some of his
friends, who were also summoned and
arrived at 8.40 o'clock."
Another surgeon and two trained
nurses meanwhile arrived from the
Naval Landing Party headquarters
and the British Consulate was also
notified of Tinkler's serious condition.
This notification was made through
the Japanese Consulate. At 10
o'clock, Tinkler was removed to the
General Hospital."
"These facts, gentlemen," the
spokesman continued, "can be checked
through the Britons who were at the
scene from the beginning of the
scuffle until they left the infirmary."
Asked as to whether he knew the
exact number of stabs sustained by
Tinkler in the fight, the spokesman
said that there were six major stabs.
A correspondent then asked whe-
ther the Japanese had taken any fur-
ther steps in connection with the in-
cident, the Embassy spokesman re-
plying that the British Consul-General
was scheduled to call on Mr. Y.
Miura, Japanese Consul-General yes-
terday but that he did not know
whether the call had actually been
made.
Asked whether any further steps
had been taken to prevent the re-
petition of similar incidents, the
spokesman said that no additional
measures had been taken and that
the Japanese authorities still stood
by the guarantee they had given on
May 23, with regard to the protection
of the plant in Pootung.

Capital and Labour

With reference to the anti-British
demonstrations which are being stag-
ed in Pootung almost daily, a cor-
respondent asked whether these were
being authorized by the Japanese
authorities.
The spokesman replied that the
Japanese forces were not there to in-
tervene in disputes between capital
and labour.
Told of persistent reports according
to which there was considerable un-
rest amongst labour employed by
British interests in Pootung and asked
whether the spokesman was aware of
any meeting which was reported to
have been held in this connection
yesterday afternoon between Com-
mander Minesuke Noji and the mana-
gers of the various British plants
having establishments in Pootung, the
spokesman said that he had spoken to
the Commandant in the morning but
that nothing was said with regard to
the proposed meeting.
pages.zh:
然而，所有其他伤口都得到了处理，这花费了大约一小时，而不是我昨天提到的三小时。随后丁克勒被送到病房，并要求他躺下。他抱怨枕头太低，于是又给他换了一个。随后两名英国人相继离开，但第三人一直待到下午3点（上海时间），当时被告知他留下来已无实际用处，于是他也回到了工厂。”

召唤朋友

发言人继续说：“有人问丁克勒是否需要什么，他要求喝一杯水，便给了他一杯。给他的水是从日本带来的，因为上海的水不够纯净。随后给伤者注射了吗啡，中午时问他是否想吃东西，但他说不饿。只要丁克勒还在浦东，一名外科医生和一名男护士就留在隔壁房间。下午5点30分（日本时间），发现他在出汗并吐血，外科医生由此推断他患有内出血。晚上8点（上海时间）未见好转，遂通知海军陆战队总部，同时给丁克勒注射了樟脑剂，并安排了两名日本女看护照料他。当被问及是否需要什么时，他说他想见见朋友，朋友们也被召唤并于8点40分到达。”

与此同时，另一名外科医生和两名受过训练的护士从海军陆战队总部赶到，英国领事馆也收到了丁克勒病情危重的通知。该通知是通过日本领事馆发出的。10点钟，丁克勒被转送至总医院。”

发言人继续说道：“绅士们，这些事实可以通过从一开始就在混战现场直到离开医务室的英国人来核实。”

当被问及是否知道丁克勒在打斗中被刺的确切次数时，发言人说有六处主要刺伤。随后一名记者询问日本方面是否就该事件采取了进一步措施，大使馆发言人回答说，英国总领事原定于昨天拜访日本总领事三浦义明先生，但他不知道这次拜访是否确实成行。

当被问及是否采取了进一步措施以防止类似事件重演时，发言人表示没有采取额外措施，日本当局仍然坚持其5月23日就保护浦东工厂所作的保证。

资本与劳工

鉴于浦东几乎每天都在举行反英示威，一名记者询问这些示威是否得到了日本当局的授权。

发言人回答说，日军并非介入资方与劳方之间的纠纷。

记者告知有关持续不断的报道，称受英国利益雇佣的浦东劳工中存在相当大的不安情绪，并询问发言人是否知晓野路美之助（Minesuke Noji）指挥官与在浦东设有机构的各家英国工厂经理之间据报于昨天下午举行的会议。发言人表示，他曾在上午与司令官交谈过，但未提及拟议中的会议。

pages.en:
After hearing the Naval spokes-
man's statement a British Consular
official stated last night that a British
Vice-Consul had been refused per-
mission to see Tinkler on Tuesday
afternoon and that at 7 p.m. the man's
condition had been reported to the
Consular authorities as improving and
that he was "all right." Additional
information that on the following
morning Tinkler would be able to
eat porridge and to see his friends
was also given at this hour, he added.
This, he said, was different from the
Japanese story that at 5.30 p.m. Tink-
ler had been found perspiring and
spitting blood.

Admiralty Spokesman Comments

Tokyo, June 8.
The incident which occurred at
the China Printing and Finishing
Company offices in Pootung, in which
Mr. Tinkler, a Briton, sustained
fatal injuries, "form a manifesta-
tion of the anti-Japanese atmosphere
in British circles at Shanghai," said
Rear-Admiral Kanazawa, spokesman
of the Admiralty, at his weekly press
conference today.
Replying to a foreign correspond-
ent, he declared that "the incident
itself is a small one," but in his
view the British people should main-
tain a calm attitude "because the
cumulative effects of such small
incidents could lead to an import-
ant development in the situation.
Rear-Admiral Kanazawa said that
he felt sorry for Mr. Tinkler, "but
deplored the incomprehensibly, out-
rageous attitude taken by him in
levelling a loaded revolver at the
Commander and other high officers
of the Japanese landing party and
actually firing one shot at them,
especially since the Japanese blue-
jackets had been maintaining peace
and order in the Lunchong Cotton
Mill area after having reached a
full understanding with the British
authorities."
There is not a single Japanese
bluejacket, he added, "but who re-
gards the attitude of Mr. Tinkler
as an insult to the Japanese Navy."
—Reuter.

Another Incident

Workers of the old Lun Chong
Cotton Mill in Pootung who recently
resumed work have again been
forced to quit as a result of yet an-
other incident in the British cotton
mill, this time involving only Chi-
nese workers and some "puppet"
police or soldiers in Pootung.
The incident, it was stated by Chi-
nese evening reports, occurred in
front of the mill on Wednesday
morning when a party of "puppet"
soldiers was alleged to have opened
fire on workers who had resumed
work, resulting in the wounding of
a worker who may die at any mo-
ment.
At the alleged instigation of the
"Workers League of the Republic
of China," a new organization started
by the Lun Chong strikers who have
issued several anti-British man-
ifestos, scores of these "puppet"
soldiers went to the old mill and
opened fire by way of intimidation,
trying to force workers to stop
working. In the confusion a worker
was so seriously wounded that he
may not live.
It was further alleged that the
league was creating more incidents
in order to aggravate the labour
situation in Pootung, planning to
hold more parades of workers.
The funeral will take place today
at 2.30 p.m. at the Hungjao Road
Cemetery and members of the Unit-
ed Services Association of which Mr.
Tinkler was one of the oldest mem-
bers will act as pallbearers. Mem-
bers of the Association are asked to
attend.

London Interested

London, June 8.
The Tinkler incident is given pro-
minence in most newspapers today,
although there is no comment.
It is regarded as a particularly
bad case in official circles, but ac-
tion on the matter awaits a Consular
report from Shanghai.—Reuter.
pages.zh:
在听取了海军发言人的声明后，一位英国领事官员昨晚表示，周二下午，一名英国副领事被拒绝探视廷克勒（Tinkler）；至晚上7时，据向领事当局报告，该男子状况好转，且“安然无恙”。他补充说，当时还提供了进一步消息，称廷克勒次日早晨将能够进食粥类并会见亲友。他说，这与日方所称下午5时30分发现廷克勒出汗并咯血的说法不同。

海军发言人评论

东京，6月8日。
海军发言人金泽少将（Rear-Admiral Kanazawa）在今日的每周新闻发布会上称，发生在浦东中国印染整理公司（China Printing and Finishing Company）办事处、导致英国人廷克勒先生受致命伤的事件，“体现了上海英界中的反日气氛”。
在回答一名外国记者的提问时，他宣称“事件本身很小”，但他认为英国人应保持冷静态度，“因为此类小事件的累积效应可能导致局势发生重大变化”。金泽少将表示，他对廷克勒先生感到遗憾，“但对他持枪指向日本登陆部队指挥官及其他高级军官并实际向他们开了一枪的这种令人费解、蛮横的态度表示痛惜，尤其是鉴于日本水兵在与英国当局达成充分谅解后，一直在隆昌棉厂区域维持治安与秩序。”
他补充说，“没有一名日本水兵不认为廷克勒先生的态度是对日本海军的侮辱。”——路透社。

另一起事件

近期复工的浦东旧隆昌棉厂工人，因英资棉厂内又发生的一起事件而再次被迫停工，此次事件仅涉及中国工人以及浦东的一些“伪”警察或士兵。
据中文晚报报道，该事件于周三早晨发生在工厂门前，据称一队“伪”军向复工工人开火，导致一名工人受伤，随时可能死亡。
据称，在由隆昌罢工者发起、并已发布数份反英宣言的新组织“中华民国工人联盟”的煽动下，数十名“伪”军前往旧厂，以恐吓为目的开火，试图迫使工人停止工作。混乱中，一名工人受重伤，可能不治身亡。
另有指控称，该联盟正在制造更多事件以加剧浦东的劳工局势，并计划举行更多的工人游行。
葬礼将于今日下午2时30分在虹桥路公墓举行，廷克勒先生作为其中最资深成员之一的联合服务协会（United Services Association）会员将担任护柩者。敬请协会会员出席。

伦敦方面关注

伦敦，6月8日。
廷克勒事件在今日大多数报纸上均占显著位置，尽管未有评论。
官方人士视此为一桩特别恶劣的案件，但对此事的行动有待上海发回的领事报告。——路透社。

中国印染整理公司45岁的英国雇员R. M. 廷克勒先生，因周二早晨在浦东与日本水兵发生冲突受伤而去世，其葬礼将于今日下午2时30分在虹桥路公墓举行。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
JUN 9 1939

ANTI-BRITISH CAMPAIGN

While for the time being certain aspects of the strike at the Lun Chong mills in Pootung cannot be dealt with as they ought, it is possible to draw attention to the strike itself and the factors behind it, for whatever may have been the reasons which led to its being called, there cannot be the slightest doubt now that this strike, and others which may be in contemplation are being fostered for what appear to be purely political ends. Without any qualification whatever it may be safely asserted that what is happening in Pootung is part and parcel of the Japanese inspired anti-British campaign which is being prosecuted with such vigour in practically all places which happen at the moment to be under Japanese control, and is one of the means by which the Japanese hope to drive British interests and traders out of China despite all the promises which have been given regarding the “scrupulous respect” which was to be paid to the rights and interests of all third party neutrals in China. The matter is one of considerable importance, not only to Britons trading and residing in China but all other foreigners as well, for they may be certain that what the Japanese are now endeavouring to do to the British they will seek to effect against those others in their turn. It is only to be expected that Britons in China would be the first attacked, for if the move were to succeed against them, the task of eradicating other foreign interests would be all the easier. The issue may for the moment be joined between the British and the Japanese, but there is every reason to believe that ultimately all foreign interests in Japanese occupied China will be similarly threatened. To make the matter quite plain the present strike in Pootung, and those which may occur in the future are not the result of the spontaneous action of the Chinese workers arising out of some fancied or real grievance, but has been carefully and sedulously fostered by Japanese agencies, as part of the general anti-British campaign, with perhaps some sordid financial end in view which it should not be difficult for the most casual reader to perceive.

With all the clamour which the Japanese make over alleged anti-Japanese activities their own conduct is open to very severe criticism. Parades of workers, such as that which occurred in Pootung on June 1 in an area completely under Japanese control, could not possibly have taken place without either the knowledge or consent of the Japanese. They could, if they had wished, have stopped it, but the fact that they allowed such a demonstration appears in a curious light when viewed in connection with other circumstances. The Japanese owned Chinese language paper, the “Sin Shun Pao,” has been enthusiastically fostering the movement, as witness these following extracts from a recent number of that newspaper:—

Workers of the China Printing & Finishing Co., at Pootung who have been leading a life like cattle under the devilish hands of British imperialists, are now engaged in a brave struggle against the management.

The only weapon which the workers possess is the strike, which is sufficient to deal a death blow to the capitalists.

Brave workers of the China Printing & Finishing Co., and members of the strike committee, this is a rare opportunity for you to struggle for your rights.

Go ahead! You are fighting for your own interests and for justice! We are looking forward to your glorious success.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年6月9日

反英运动

虽然目前无法以应有的方式处理浦东隆昌纱厂罢工的某些方面，但有可能提请人们注意罢工本身及其背后的因素，因为无论导致罢工号召的原因是什么，现在毫无疑问的是，这次罢工以及其他可能在酝酿中的罢工，正为了看似纯粹的政治目的而受到扶植。可以毫不保留地断言，浦东正在发生的事情是日本煽动的反英运动的一部分和整体，该运动在日本目前控制的所有地方都在大力推行，也是日本希望将英国利益和商人赶出中国的手段之一，尽管日本曾就对中国境内所有第三方中立国的权利和利益给予“谨慎尊重”作出过各种承诺。此事不仅对在华贸易和居住的英国人至关重要，对所有其他外国人也是如此，因为他们可以肯定，日本人现在试图对英国人做的事情，迟早也会施加到其他人身上。预计在华英国人将首先受到攻击，因为如果这一举动对他们成功，那么根除其他外国利益的任务就会容易得多。目前的问题可能仅限于英国和日本之间，但有充分理由相信，最终日本占领下的中国所有外国利益都将受到同样的威胁。为了把事情说得十分清楚，目前在浦东的罢工以及未来可能发生的罢工，并非中国工人因某种想象或真实的委屈而自发行动的结果，而是作为全面反英运动的一部分，由日本机构精心且不懈地扶植的，其中或许还夹杂着一些卑劣的经济目的，即使是最漫不经心的读者也不难察觉。

尽管日本人大肆喧嚷所谓的反日活动，但他们自己的行为却招致严厉批评。像6月1日在完全处于日本控制下的浦东地区发生的工人游行这类活动，若没有日本的知情或同意，根本不可能发生。如果他们愿意，本可以阻止它，但结合其他情况来看，他们允许此类示威的事实显得颇为蹊跷。日资中文报纸《新顺报》一直在热情地鼓吹这一运动，该报最近一期中的以下摘录可为佐证：—

在帝国主义魔鬼般的魔掌下过着牛马般生活的浦东中国印染整理公司工人，现在正与管理层进行英勇的斗争。

工人拥有的唯一武器就是罢工，这足以给资本家以致命一击。

中国印染整理公司的勇敢工人们，以及罢工委员会的成员们，这是你们为权利而斗争的难得机会。

前进吧！你们是在为自己的利益和正义而战！我们期待着你们的光荣胜利。

pages.en:
Sentiments of such a nature as these, reek-
ing with the spirit of communism which
Japan is supposed to be wiping out of China,
reads strangely in a newspaper owned by
Japanese, and suggests that “dangerous
thoughts” can, and do form a portion of the
weapons to which the Japanese inspirers of
these disorders will willingly resort if it
suits their book. It may be taken for grant-
ed that if the above extracts appeared in any
other foreign owned Chinese language paper
levelled against any Japanese industrial con-
cern in Shanghai or the neighbourhood,
Japanese indignation would be raised to
fever pitch, though it seems to be perfectly
all right so far as the Japanese are concern-
ed if such sentiments are voiced against any
of the third party neutrals trading in China.
What may be perfectly good sauce for the
British goose, is by no means a fit condiment
for the Japanese gander, or at least that is
how the situation for the moment presents
itself.
But what of the innocent Chinese who
are allowing themselves to be deluded by
such propaganda? They do not appear to
realize that, by striking in the manner they
are, they are playing into the hands of that
nation, which only recently detailed the mil-
lions of Chinese soldiers reported to have
been killed during the last twenty-three
months of hostilities. They appear to have
forgotten that, only a very short while ago,
death and destruction were rained upon them
and their fellows in the very areas in which
they are now living by these people who now
seek to induce them to follow certain courses,
not for their own benefit, but for the benefit
of the Japanese who have wrought so great
an evil in this country. They are allowing
themselves to be made the catspaws with
which Japan is endeavouring to pull those
particular chestnuts which she fancies out of
the fire, and are being seduced into a line
of action which betrays the best interests of
their own country. Were the Japanese able
to drive foreign interests out of the country,
and it is not to be believed, fortunately, that
they will succeed, do these misguided Chinese
believe for one moment that their lot would
be any better? The designs for exploitation
of the Chinese which the Japanese undoubt-
edly have in their mind, can only succeed
with the removal of competition for Chinese
labour, and if that is ever removed the
Chinese worker will be reduced to the posi-
tion of a sweated helot, on a bare subsist-
ence wage and without a soul to call his
own. The absence of competition in the
labour market must ultimately mean the
reduction of wages, and descent to an even
poorer standard of living than even now
prevails, and it follows that the elimination
of existing foreign interests must in the long
run militate against the interests of the
Chinese workers themselves. That is a
point which should be brought home to the
strikers, and all other Chinese who may be
induced to follow their example. They are,
whether they intend to do so or not, in fact
playing the game as the Japanese want it
played, and probably quite unwittingly are
assisting the enemies of their country who has
brought about such destruction and destitu-
tion wherever their armies have passed.
What is more they are pickling a rod for
their own chastisement, a thing which not
even the most misguided worker wishes to do.
pages.zh:
这类充满共产主义气息的情感言论，出现在一家日资报纸上显得格外怪异，毕竟日本声称正在清除中国的共产主义；这表明，“危险思想”确实构成了这些骚乱的日本煽动者乐意使用的武器的一部分，只要符合他们的利益。可以想见，如果上述摘录出现在任何其他外资中文报纸上，针对上海或附近的任何日本工业企业，日本人的愤怒将会达到沸点；然而，当这些言论针对在中国贸易的任何第三方中立国时，日本人似乎觉得完全没问题。对英国雌鹅适用的酱料，绝不适合日本雄鹅，至少目前的局势呈现如此。

但是，那些任由自己受此类宣传蒙蔽的无辜中国人又如何呢？他们似乎没有意识到，以这种方式罢工，他们正是在帮那个国家的忙，而就在最近，该国还详细列出了在过去二十三个月的敌对行动中据报道被杀死的数百万中国士兵。他们似乎忘记了，就在不久前，正是这些现在试图诱导他们采取某些行动的人，在他们目前生活的地区，给他们及其同胞带来了死亡和毁灭；这些人这样做并非为了中国人的利益，而是为了给在这个国家造成巨大罪恶的日本谋利。他们任由自己被当作替日本从火中取出其所觊觎栗子的猫爪，并被诱骗采取违背本国最佳利益的行动。如果日本人能够将外国利益赶出该国——幸运的是，人们不相信他们会成功——这些迷途的中国人会相信他们的处境会有丝毫改善吗？日本人心目中无疑有的剥削中国人的计划，只有在消除对中国劳动力的竞争后才能成功；如果这种竞争被消除，中国工人将沦为仅得糊口工资、毫无自主权的受压榨农奴。劳动力市场竞争的缺失最终必然意味着工资降低，生活水平降至比现在更贫困的标准，因此，现有外国利益的消除从长远来看必将损害中国工人自身的利益。这一点应向罢工者及所有可能被诱导效仿的其他中国人讲明。无论他们是否有意，事实上他们正在按照日本人的意愿行事，并且可能在不知不觉中协助了他们的国家敌人，而这些敌人的军队所到之处，只带来破坏和贫困。更重要的是，他们这是在为自己招致惩罚，即便是最迷途的工人也不愿这样做。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
JUN 7 1939
Lun Chong Man
Dies Of Wounds
After Operation
Consulate Takes Grave
View Of Incident;
Protest Seen
BRITON SUCCUMBS
TO BAYONET CUTS
Inquest Begins; Body
Formally Identified;
Autopsy Held
British Consular officials
this morning were consider-
ing the whole Tinkler affair
very seriously, and it is ex-
pected that a strong protest
will be made to the Japanese
authorities on the grounds
of their unnecessarily strong
action against Mr. Tinkler,
and because of their delin-
quence in not having allowed
him to be sent to Shanghai
immediately for first-class
medical attention.
It appears that Mr. Tinkler,
acting under great stress of
mind, probably lost his temper
in the mix-up at the Lun
Chong Mill yesterday morning,
and was finally disarmed by
Japanese sailors. It has not
been established whether he re-
ceived his bayonet wounds before
or after he was disarmed.
Released Too Late
Only released by the Japanese
naval forces in Pootung when
his condition became very
serious last night, Mr. Richard
Maurice Tinkler of the China
Printing and Finishing Company's
Pootung Works was operated upon
at midnight in the General Hos-
pital, but died at 5.30 a.m.
Mr. Tinkler was wounded at 8
a.m. yesterday, when Japanese
sailors bayonetted him twice in the
abdomen, causing serious abdo-
minal wounds, and wounded him
also in the scalp and leg, after
he had allegedly brandished a
pistol and fired a shot at a Japan-
ese naval officer. This took place
after strikers had demonstrated
at the plant, and the Japanese
landing party had come on the
scene.
Incident Regretted
Sir Herbert Phillips, British
Consul-General, yesterday ex-
pressed his regrets to the Japan-
ese Consul-General that the affair
should have happened. The
management of Lun Chong did
the same, while definitely point-
ing out that Mr. Tinkler was act-
ing in the best interests of the
company yesterday morning in
preventing strikers from damag-
ing the company's property.
The affair took place about 8
a.m., and Mr. Tinkler was arrest-
ed by the Japanese and held in-
communicado at Pootung, where
he was placed in a crude hospital.
It appeared that the Japanese
yesterday intended to hold Tinkler
and not hand him over to the
British authorities despite his
critical condition.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. E. No. 9. D. 69684 8/6 39）
（批：R 8/6 file 8/6）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》。
1939年6月7日
伦崇曼
术后伤重
身亡
领事馆严肃看待
此事；预计将提出
抗议
英国人死于
刺刀创伤
死因研讯开始；遗体
正式确认；进行尸检

英国领事官员今晨正极为严肃地审议整个廷克勒（Tinkler）事件，预计将以日本当局对廷克勒先生采取不必要的过激行动，以及因其失职未允许立即将其送往上海接受一流医疗救治为由，向日本当局提出强烈抗议。

看来，廷克勒先生在昨天上午伦崇纱厂的混乱中，因精神极度紧张，可能失去了理智，最终被日本水兵缴械。目前尚不清楚他是在被缴械之前还是之后遭受刺刀创伤的。

释放过迟

中国印刷整理公司浦东工厂的理查德·莫里斯·廷克勒（Richard Maurice Tinkler）先生直到昨晚病情非常严重时，才被驻浦东的日本海军部队释放。他于午夜在总医院接受手术，但于凌晨5时30分去世。

廷克勒先生于昨天上午8时受伤，当时据称他挥舞手枪并向一名日本海军军官开了一枪，随后日本水兵用刺刀两次刺入其腹部，造成严重的腹部创伤，并致其头皮和腿部受伤。此事发生在罢工者在工厂示威以及日本登陆部队抵达现场之后。

对事件表示遗憾

英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）昨日向日本总领事表示，对发生此事感到遗憾。伦崇纱厂管理层也表达了同样的遗憾，同时明确指出，廷克勒先生昨天上午的行为是为了防止罢工者破坏公司财产，符合公司的最大利益。

事件发生在上午8时左右，廷克勒先生被日本人逮捕，并在浦东被单独拘禁，那里只有一所简陋的医院。看来，日本人昨天意图扣留廷克勒，尽管他病情危重，也不将其移交给英国当局。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 S. E. No. 9. D. 69684 8/6 39）
（批：R 8/6 卷宗 8/6）

pages.en:
Wounds Underestimated
A Japanese doctor attended him,
and told inquirers that Mr.
Tinkler's wounds were not serious.
Last night, however, when two
members of the British Consulate
staff went to Pootung, the Japan-
ese allowed him to be taken to
Shanghai, lending every assis-
tance, as they realized then that
he was in a serious condition.
Dr. W. Korec, German, and Dr.
Reidar Sundsbak, Norwegian,
operated from midnight until 3
a.m. at the General Hospital, and
realized that Mr. Tinkler had little
chance, due to the delay of 15
hours. The two abdominal wounds
had caused many injuries to the
intestines and bowels, causing
haemhorrage and great loss of
blood. He died at 5.30 a.m.
Inquest Opened
The inquest was opened at the
General Hospital mortuary this
morning by Mr. C. H. Haines, Re-
gistrar of HBM Court, sitting as
Coroner. Formal evidence of
identification was given by Mr. R.
Cowan, director of the China
Printing & Finishing Company,
and the inquest was adjourned
until today week.
A former inspector of the Shang-
hai Municipal Police, and holder
of the British Distinguished Con-
duct Medal for gallantry in the
Great War, when he served in the
Royal Fusiliers, Mr. Tinkler was a
native of Grange-over-Sands, Lan-
cashire. He had been in the em-
ploy of the China Printing and
Finishing Company for some years,
and was 45 years of age.
An autopsy was held following
the opening of the inquest. It
was carried out by Dr. I. G. Ander-
son, of the "M" firm of doctors.
pages.zh:
伤势被低估

一名日本医生为他诊治，并告诉询问者说，廷克勒先生的伤势并不严重。然而，昨晚当两名英国领事馆工作人员前往浦东时，日本人意识到他病情严重，便提供了一切协助，允许将他送往上海。

德国医生W. Korec博士和挪威医生Reidar Sundsbak博士在总医院从午夜一直手术到凌晨3时，他们意识到由于延误了15个小时，廷克勒先生生还的希望渺茫。两处腹部伤口导致肠道多处损伤，引起出血和大量失血。他于凌晨5时30分死亡。

死因研讯开启

英王陛下法院书记官兼验尸官C. H. Haines先生今晨在总医院停尸房开启了死因研讯。中国印刷整理公司董事R. Cowan先生提供了正式的身份确认证据，研讯休庭至下周同日。

廷克勒先生是兰开夏郡格兰奇奥弗桑兹（Grange-over-Sands）人，曾任上海公共租界工部局警务处巡长，并在第一次世界大战期间服役于皇家燧发枪团（Royal Fusiliers），因英勇表现获得英国杰出行为勋章（Distinguished Conduct Medal）。他受雇于中国印刷整理公司已数年，享年45岁。

死因研讯开始后进行了尸检。尸检由“M”医生事务所的I. G. Anderson博士执行。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
14920
JUN 7 1939

Japanese Give
View On Tinkler

Consular Official Says
Surprised Briton
Not Shot

Actions of R. M. Tinkler, 45-year-old employee of the China Printing and Finishing Company at the firm's Pootung Point works on Tuesday morning, constituted "a deliberate insult" to the Japanese Navy, Mr. Zen Tsurumi, spokesman for the Japanese Consulate-General in Shanghai, said today.

"This is not an issue involving the pointing of a gun by a Briton towards a Japanese," he said. "It involves an act of lawlessness towards officers in uniform. Hence its extreme gravity."

Mr. Tsurumi expressed surprise that Tinkler had "not been shot and killed on the spot."

Protection

The spokesman recalled that the Japanese Naval Landing Party had stationed a force at the mill on May 24 following a request by the British Consulate-General for measures to protect the property in view of the prevailing strike.

"Yesterday," he continued, "When a dispute arose between strikers and non-strikers, the Japanese Naval Landing Party did its best to suppress the disturbance.

Arrogance

"At this time, trouble arose between the British employees of the plant and the landing party. One Briton from this group, displaying an extremely arrogant attitude, went about pointing a gun to Japanese section, company and battalion commanders. He even fired a shot.

"This was a grave provocation towards the Japanese Navy. It is not difficult to imagine the indignation his actions gave rise to among the men who saw their superior officers being insulted.

"That they should have disarmed this dangerous character in self-defense and that they should have subsequently manhandled him is only natural under the circumstances, the consular spokesman declared.

Makeshift Settlement

An "indefinite and makeshift" settlement of the Anglo-Japanese incident at the China Printing and Finishing Company's Pootung Point plant in which R. M. Tinkler was alleged to have fired a pistol at a Japanese bluejacket and subsequently threatened Japanese officers with his weapon "cannot be tolerated," the Taiiku Shimpo, local Japanese daily, declared in an editorial today.

"The firing of a gun at the Japanese military within Japanese occupied territory is a case of unprecedented gravity," the newspaper said.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》。
14920
1939年6月7日

日本方面就
廷克勒事件
发表看法

领事官员称
惊讶于该英国人
未被击毙

上海日本总领事馆发言人鹤见善（Zen Tsurumi，音译）今日表示，周二上午，中国印刷整理公司浦东尖角工厂45岁的雇员R. M. 廷克勒的行为构成了对日本海军的“故意侮辱”。

“这不仅仅是一个英国人用枪指着日本人的问题，”他说。“这是针对身穿制服的军官的无法无天的行为。因此其性质极其严重。”

鹤见先生对廷克勒“未被当场击毙”表示惊讶。

保护

该发言人回顾说，鉴于当时的罢工情况，应英国总领事馆关于采取措施保护财产的要求，日本海军陆战队已于5月24日在该纱厂部署了兵力。

“昨天，”他继续说，“当罢工者与未罢工者之间发生纠纷时，日本海军陆战队尽力平息骚乱。

傲慢

“此时，工厂的英国雇员与登陆部队之间发生了冲突。这群人中的一名英国人以极其傲慢的态度，拿着枪指向日本的分队长、连长和营长。他甚至开了一枪。

“这是对日本海军的严重挑衅。不难想象，他的行为在目睹上级军官受辱的士兵中引起了怎样的愤怒。

“领事馆发言人宣称，在这种情况下，他们出于自卫解除这个危险人物的武装，并随后对他进行粗暴对待，是合乎情理的。

临时解决

当地日文日报《体育新闻》（Taiiku Shimpo，音译）今日在一篇社论中宣称，对于在中国印刷整理公司浦东尖角工厂发生的英日事件——据称R. M. 廷克勒向一名日本水兵开枪，并随后用武器威胁日本军官——这种“不确定且临时凑合”的解决办法是“不能容忍的”。

该报称：“在日本占领区内向日本军队开枪，是前所未有的严重事件。”

pages.en:
14921

“Hoodlums”
The Japanese authorities were urged by the journal to face the issue with a firm determination, so that the indignation caused by the affair among the local Japanese residents shall not be in vain.”
“The Britons who caused the present incident may be hoodlums hired by the company as strike breakers. But that is not the point. They may be uneducated hoodlums but their impertinence and violence represents the contempt and enmity of Britons as a whole towards Japan,” the Tairiku Shimpo declared.
The case, the newspaper declared,” is gaining gravity as a deliberate insult and provocation of the British towards the Japanese armed forces.”
Previous Assurance
“As the Japanese Naval Landing Party, in keeping with its previous assurances, moved to curb violence by the strikers, employees of the firm returned kindness with insults and threats instead of gratitude. Moreover using a firearm which should not have been there, an attempt was made by an employee to shoot a Japanese bluejacket. This was not a mistake, but an insult and a provocation. It should be treated by the Japanese authorities as a challenge,” the newspaper declared.
The firm management, the Tairiku Shimpo declared, had expressed its regrets and apologies, while Sir Herbert Phillips, the British Consul-General, had expressed his regrets that the incident should have occurred when a protest was lodged by Japanese Consul-General Yoshiaki Miura, on Tuesday.
“But as stated before this was not an accident or a mistake. Should this case be settled as in the past with a mere apology and assurance against a future repetition is to be feared that a grave source of danger for the future will be left,” the newspaper declared.
pages.zh:
14921

“流氓”

该报敦促日本当局以坚定的决心面对这一问题，以免当地日本居民因此事产生的愤慨落空。”
《大陆新报》（Tairiku Shimpo，音译）宣称：“引发当前事件的英国人可能是公司雇佣的破坏罢工的流氓。但这不是重点。他们可能是没受过教育的流氓，但他们的无礼和暴力代表了全体英国人对日本的蔑视和敌意。”
该报宣称，随着此案被视为英国人对日本武装部队的故意侮辱和挑衅，其严重性正在增加。

先前的保证

该报宣称：“正如日本海军陆战队按照其先前的保证，采取行动遏制罢工者的暴力行为一样，该公司员工非但没有感激，反而以侮辱和威胁回报。此外，一名员工试图使用本不该出现的枪支射击一名日本水兵。这不是失误，而是侮辱和挑衅。日本当局应将其视为一种挑战。”

《大陆新报》宣称，公司管理层已表示遗憾和道歉，而英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士则在周二日本总领事三浦义明（Yoshiaki Miura，音译）提出抗议时，对发生此事表示了遗憾。

“但如前所述，这并非意外或失误。如果此案像过去那样仅以道歉和保证不再重犯来了结，恐怕会留下未来严重的危险根源，”该报宣称。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

（印：POLICE S. I. REGISTRY No. S. R. D. 6968 A Date ... 39）

JUN 6 1939

Tinkler, Lun Chong
Employee Arrested;
“Fired On” Japanese

R. M. Tinkler, 45, an employee of the Cotton Mill of the China Printing and Finishing Company, at Pootung Point, was arrested by the Japanese Naval Landing Party this morning after allegedly firing a shot at a Japanese officer commanding a landing party in the area.

Winkler was also accused of having threatened Lieut.-Commander Munesuke Noji, commandant of the Japanese naval landing party in Pootung, with his pistol, and to have behaved in a similar manner towards another Japanese naval officer.

Investigation
Officials of Lun Chong are to investigate the affair this afternoon. At the time of going to press there is no confirmation of Mr. Tinkler having fired a shot.

Lieutenant Commander Noji is the same officer who accused a Seaforth sentry of having wounded him with a bayonet recently, although it is reported that he placed his hand on the bayonet and cut it when the sentry naturally pulled away.

（批：Liu 8/6 R up E. ½）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》。

（印：警务处 S. I. 登记处 No. S. R. D. 6968 A 日期 ... 39）

1939年6月6日

廷克勒，伦崇
雇员被捕；
“向”日本人“开枪”

R. M. 廷克勒，45岁，中国印刷整理公司位于浦东尖角的棉纺厂雇员，今晨被日本海军陆战队逮捕，原因是据称他向指挥该地区登陆部队的一名日本军官开了一枪。

廷克勒还被指控用手枪威胁驻浦东的日本海军陆战队指挥官野次 Munessuke（Noji，音译）少佐，并对另一名日本海军军官表现出类似的行为。

调查

伦崇纱厂官员将于今天下午调查此事。截至发稿时，尚未证实廷克勒先生开了枪。

野次（Noji）少佐就是最近指控一名海福尔（Seaforth，音译）哨兵用刺刀刺伤他的同一名军官，尽管有报道称，当哨兵本能地抽回刺刀时，是他把手放在刺刀上割伤的。

（批：Liu 8/6 R up E. ½）

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
14160
JUN 6 1939

Reading
The
News
By JOHN AHLERS

WITHIN a short time, the
second western-owned enter-
prise in Pootung has become the
target of a violent labor move-
ment. First the strike in the
Lun Chong factory was engineer-
ed, and then a small strike was
also staged in the Mackenzie &
Company godown. So-called
"workers' leagues" sponsored by
the made-in-Japan "Shanghai
City Government" appear to be
behind the trouble, and thus it is
not to be wondered at that strikes
were brought about only in west-
ern-owned and not in Japanese-
managed firms. As far as the in-
stigators of the movement are
concerned, they obviously have in
mind a new anti-western intrigue,
calculated to disturb the good
local understanding between the
westerners and the Chinese in
general.

Wage Adjustment
On the other hand, the trouble
makers might abuse real griev-
ances of the laborers involved in
these strikes. We do not know
what wages are being paid in the
Pootung enterprises concerned,
and how these wages compare
with pre-war times and the re-
cent enormous rise in the cost of
living in Shanghai. It has been
said that the two Pootung firms
hit by the strikes pay particular-
ly good wages.
On the whole, however, it is
obvious that in most enterprises
in Shanghai the adjustment of
wages and salaries to the increas-
ed cost of living, and the devalua-
tion of Chinese currency, is
lagging far behind the situation
and that a large part of some ex-
traordinarily high profits recently
reported were due to insufficient
or retarded wage increases. To
forestall future trouble, the S.M.C.
ought to investigate the matter
in time and do something about
it.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》。
14160
1939年6月6日

阅读
新闻
作者：JOHN AHLERS

短时间内，浦东第二家西方拥有的企业成为了激烈劳工运动的目标。先是伦崇工厂的罢工被策划，接着麦肯锡公司（Mackenzie & Company）仓库也上演了一场小规模罢工。由日本制造的“上海市政府”赞助的所谓“工人联盟”似乎是幕后推手，因此罢工只发生在西方拥有而非日本管理的企业中也就不足为奇了。就运动的煽动者而言，他们显然心怀新的反西方阴谋，旨在扰乱西方人与一般中国人之间良好的本地关系。

工资调整

另一方面，麻烦制造者可能会利用涉及这些罢工的工人的真实不满。我们不知道相关浦东企业支付的工资是多少，以及这些工资与战前水平和上海近期生活成本的巨大上涨相比如何。据说，遭受罢工打击的两家浦东公司支付的工资特别好。

然而，总体而言，很明显，在上海的大多数企业中，工资和薪金的调整远远落后于生活成本增加和中国货币贬值的形势，最近报道的一些异常高的利润中，有很大一部分是由于工资增长不足或滞后造成的。为了预防未来的麻烦，工部局应及时调查此事并采取行动。

pages.en:
14161

Japanese Employment
The local Japanese community
substantially improved its employ
ment status last month, loca:
Nipponese papers report. Early
in May, measures had been taken
to reduce the influx of jobless
newcomers from Japan, and a
drive to provide unemployed
Japanese here with jobs was car
ried out. As a result, local Japan-
ese unemployment, which has
been considerable in April, dis-
appeared last months when jobs
offered to Japanese became more
numerous than Japanese applying
for jobs, the local Japanese Re-
sidents' Corporation reports.
On June 1, 1939, Japanese
civilians in Shanghai numbered
44,851 whereof 25,776 were male
and 19,075 females. These figures
are still at a great distance from
the hypothetical figure of 300,000
for the local Nipponese community
as calculated in recent made-in-
Japan plans for future "Greater
Shanghai."

Ningpo-Wenchow
The Chinese military authorities
in Chekiang Province have again
revised their list of goods allowed
for shipment to Shanghai from
Ningpo and Wenchow. The list
in its present form includes wood
oil, cotton, tea, raw silk and a
series of other products which for
some time had been refused per-
mits for shipment to Shanghai.
If the Japanese bombing opera-
tions against Ningpo and Wen-
chow do not prove too great an
obstacle, produce arrivals here
from those two ports ought to
increase in the near future.
pages.zh:
14161

日本人就业情况
据当地日文报纸报道，上月当地日本侨民社区的就业状况有了显著改善。五月初，已采取措施减少来自日本的失业新移民的涌入，并开展了一项为当地失业日本人提供工作的行动。据当地日本居留民团报告，结果，四月份相当严重的当地日本人失业现象在上月消失，当时提供给日本人的工作岗位数量超过了申请工作的日本人数量。
1939年6月1日，上海的日本平民人数为44,851人，其中男性25,776人，女性19,075人。这些数字与日本近期制定的未来“大上海”计划中推算的当地日本侨民社区30万人的假设数字仍相去甚远。

宁波—温州
浙江省中国军事当局再次修订了允许从宁波和温州运往上海的货物清单。目前的清单包括桐油、棉花、茶叶、生丝以及一系列其他产品，这些产品在一段时间内曾被拒绝发给运往上海的许可证。如果日军对宁波和温州的轰炸行动不构成太大障碍，预计近期从这两个港口抵达此地的农产品将会增加。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
S. D. 13960
No. S. A D. 6968 A

JUN 2 1938

Anti-British Parade
In Pootung
Demonstrators March
Through Streets

An anti-British parade in which more than 1,000 persons, reported to be workers of the Lun Chong Cotton Mill in Pootung, who have been on strike was held in Pootung on Wednesday morning. Anti-British slogans were shouted and the parade traversed several main streets on the peninsula where British and other foreign factories are located.

A review of the slogans as published by the "Sin Shun Pao" yesterday reveals that those in the parade were extremely anti-British. Although the report asserted that the demonstrators are workers of the Lun Chong Cotton Mill another Chinese report stated that they are loafers. indicating official support, the parade started from the front door of the Political Administrator's Office in Pootung under the supervision of the Chinese police.

Some of the slogans published state: "We strike because it is holy and sacred and let's be united against the British"; "The British have ill-treated Chinese workers and therefore they are the public enemies of the Chinese." "British capitalists are ghosts who absorb our blood and sweat," "The Workers League of the Republic of China is the headquarters of workers which gives protection to workers," "British factories are tools of economic aggression," and "Ill-treatment of Chinese workers has revealed the true complexion of British imperialists."

FILE
Q
C 2/6 7/6
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，
S. D. 13960
编号 S. A D. 6968 A

1938年6月2日

浦东反英游行
示威者沿街行进

周三上午，浦东举行了一场反英游行，据报道有一千多人参加，他们是浦东伦钟棉纺厂（Lun Chong Cotton Mill）的罢工工人。游行中高呼反英口号，队伍 traversed（穿过）了该半岛上英国及其他外国工厂所在的几条主要街道。

根据昨日《申报》刊登的口号回顾，游行参与者表现出极端的反英情绪。尽管报道声称示威者是伦钟棉纺厂的工人，但另一份中文报告称他们是无业游民。在当局的默许下，游行在中国警察的监视下，从浦东政治专员公署的大门前出发。

部分刊登的口号如下：“我们罢工是神圣庄严的，让我们团结起来反对英国人”；“英国人虐待中国工人，因此他们是中国人民的公敌。”“英国资本家是吸吮我们血汗的鬼魂”，“中华民国工人联盟是保护工人的工人总部”，“英国工厂是经济侵略的工具”，以及“虐待中国工人暴露了英国帝国主义者的真面目”。

CHINA PRESS.
13904
JUN 2 1939

Lun Chong Mill
Negotiations
In Progress

Puppets Said Fanning
Anti - British Feeling
At Demonstrations

Negotiations between officials of
the China Finishing and Printing
Company and representatives of the
striking workers in the firm's Poo-
tung factories were still in progress,
THE CHINA PRESS learned yesterday.
While it was too early to predict
the outcome of the conference, it
was authoritatively stated that both
sides were anxious to bring the dis-
pute to a satisfactory settlement in
the nearest future.

Interviewed by a reporter of
this journal, an employee of the
British company stated that
"In order to fan up anti-British
feelings, the puppets are or-
ganizing all sorts of parades and
demonstrations with not a few
of the workers falling into the
trap."

Commenting on a report in the
puppet-owned Chinese language
paper that two mammoth parades
were held in Pootung on Wednes-
day, the informant stated that only
a small portion of the participants
could be identified as employees of
the British mills.

"The parades were no manifesta-
tion for higher pay and better
treatment" he asserted, "they were
purely anti-British demonstrations."

Posters bearing anti-British
slogans were said to have been
seen everywhere in the Jap-
anese-occupied areas around the
Settlement and Concession,
while puppet orators appeared
before large gatherings charg-
ing his audiences to "breakdown
British imperialism."

According to a report in a pro-
Japanese Chinese language paper,
the "workers" adopted ten resolu-
tions, each of which was anti-Bri-
tish in nature.

The first of the resolution is
typical. It stated that "because the
British mistreated our fellow work-
ers, they are the common enemy
of the Chinese people."

《大美晚报》
13904
1939年6月2日

伦钟纱厂
谈判
进行中

据称傀儡政权在示威活动中煽动
反英情绪

《大美晚报》记者昨日获悉，中国印染整理公司（China Finishing and Printing Company）官员与其浦东工厂罢工工人代表之间的谈判仍在进行中。虽然预测会议结果还为时过早，但有权威人士指出，双方都迫切希望在不久的将来将争端达成满意的解决。

本报记者在采访一位英资公司雇员时，该雇员表示：“为了煽动反英情绪，傀儡们正在组织各种游行和示威活动，不少工人落入圈套。”

针对一家由傀儡控制的中文报纸关于周三在浦东举行了两次大规模游行的报道，该消息人士称，只有少数参与者能被确认为英资纱厂的员工。

他断言：“这些游行并非为了争取更高工资和更好待遇的表现，它们纯粹是反英示威。”

据说在租界及公共租界周边日占区，到处都能看到张贴着反英标语的海报，同时傀儡政权的演说家出现在大型集会上，鼓动听众“打倒英国帝国主义”。

据一份亲日中文报纸报道，这些“工人”通过了十项决议，每一项都具有反英性质。

第一项决议颇具代表性。声明称：“由于英国人虐待我们的工友，他们是中国人民的共同敌人。”

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JUN 1 1939

（批：13731 □□ 6765 A 1 27）

Strike at Lun Chong Mill Continues
Pickets Act to Prevent Men Returning to Work

The strike at the Lun Chong Cotton Mill, Pootung, in which pickets organized by strikers alleged to have been politically inspired prevented workers from going to work on Monday, may be settled through diplomatic channels the management having made a report to the British Consulate-General, according to a Chinese report. Workers are stated to be willing to resume work.
It will be recalled that when the workers tried to return to work on Monday they were stopped from doing so by pickets appointed by the Lun Chong Workers League who travelled in sampans. As a result of their interference, only a few hundred workers could enter the mill but since the mill employs more than 2,000 workers it was forced to suspend operations pending the final settlement of the trouble.

（批：File R 1/6 □□）

《字林西报》，

1939年6月1日

（批注：13731 □□ 6765 A 1 27）

伦钟纱厂罢工持续
纠察队阻止工人复工

据一份中文报道，浦东伦钟棉纺厂的罢工可能通过外交渠道解决，厂方已向英国总领事馆提交报告。周一，据称受政治煽动的罢工者组织的纠察队阻止工人上班。据悉工人们愿意复工。
回想起来，当工人们周一试图返回工作时，被伦钟工人联盟指派乘坐舢板前来的纠察队阻止。由于他们的干扰，只有几百名工人能够进入工厂，但由于该厂雇佣了2000多名工人，被迫暂停运营，等待纠纷的最终解决。

（批注：File R 1/6 □□）

伦钟罢工者
复工

《字林西报》获悉，自5月20日星期六以来一直在浦东角（Pootung Point）中国印染整理公司伦钟纱厂罢工的若干中国雇员，于昨日复工。然而，据称该厂仍由接替海福斯高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）的日军士兵守卫。

《上海泰晤士报》，

1939年5月20日

伦钟纱厂作业
昨日重启

大量2000名员工在中文报纸刊登广告后返岗；煽动者被解雇

据昨日权威消息，居住在租界及华界的伦钟棉纺厂（位于浦东）的2000名员工中的大部分于昨日上午返岗工作。当然，也有部分员工居住在浦东和虹口。居住在这一侧（指租界一侧）的员工每天早晨由公司私人运营的两艘大型舢板从外白渡桥运送至工厂。然而，在这两家工厂（制造部和棉整部）工作的全部2000名员工并未全部报到，但相信其余人员很快就会回到工作岗位。该厂员工自5月20日起一直罢工。
据称，此次罢工的煽动者约有20人，公司在任何情况下都肯定不会重新雇用他们。据称，一些被指控煽动的人自1934年工厂在此开业以来一直受雇于该公司，曾经是优秀的工人，但他们将从公司的工资单上除名。
报纸广告显示
伦钟纱厂由中国印染整理有限公司（China Printing and Finishing Co., Ltd.）拥有和经营。该公司上周五在中文报纸上刊登广告，声明纱厂将重新开始运营，老员工如果愿意可以返岗工作。昨天，大量员工重返岗位，工厂再次开始运转。
该厂共雇佣约60名外国人。其中大多数是来自英国兰开夏郡纺织企业的英国纺织专家和技术人员。这里也雇佣了几名俄罗斯人担任监工和机械师。
当煽动活动猖獗时，给予该厂的英国海军和军事保护已于5月23日撤销，此前日本当局保证他们将负责保护占领区内工厂的安全。自5月23日以来，日本海军陆战队一直驻扎在该处。
许多人住在租界
许多伦钟纱厂员工……（原文此处有残缺或排版混乱，根据上下文推测意为：许多伦钟纱厂员工居住在租界……）
市长抗议
关于在伦钟浦东角工厂罢工后派遣英国军队一事，上海市特别市市长傅筱庵先生昨日向英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）发出了一份措辞强烈的正式照会。
“傅先生要求英国当局保证，英国军队将尊重上海市特别市的管辖权并维护和平与秩序，且今后不再采取此类行动。傅先生强调，如果将来发生类似事件，由此产生的后果责任应由英国驻军承担。傅先生认为，在未事先通知上海市特别市当局的情况下派遣英国军队，是对其管辖权的蔑视。”
在日本当局提出抗议后，英军立即撤离。

Special Branch, S.5
REPORT
Date May 20, 1939
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. S. D. 6768 Station 39）

Subject Labour Dispute in the China Printing & Finishing Works - Pootung.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S. McKeown

At 9.55 p.m. May 20, the following message was received through C.C.R.:-

From C.P. to Special Branch:

The British Consul-General telephoned and informed Municipal Police that there is trouble in the China Printing & Finishing Works, Pootung. This appears to be a labour dispute. Japanese has been requested to use Pootung Police. In the meantime British Naval Guard has been landed on Pootung side at the Works. Watch the developments if any information of importance is obtained on this side of the river inform British Consul-General.

The D.C. (Special Branch) was informed. C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang stated that no information on the dispute was available and that none could be obtained until it was possible for an agent to proceed to Pootung. Mr. Brown of the company was communicated with and informed that the Special Branch would render assistance if necessary on this side of the river. Later Mr. Brown passed on the information that the trouble arose when the workers who for some time had been involved with the management over a labour dispute refused to leave the factory at 5 p.m., the usual time and adopted a threatening attitude. 日期：1939年5月20日
（印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. S. D. 6768 Station 39）

主题：中国印染整理厂（浦东）的劳资纠纷。

撰写及呈报人：D.S. McKeown

5月20日晚9点55分，通过中央无线电接收室（C.C.R.）收到以下信息：-

从中央巡捕房（C.P.）致特务科：

英国总领事打电话通知警务处，浦东中国印染整理厂发生骚乱。这似乎是一起劳资纠纷。已请求日本人使用浦东警力。与此同时，英国海军警卫队已在该厂浦东一侧登陆。请密切关注事态发展，如果在河这边获得任何重要信息，请通知英国总领事。

特务科副科长（D.C.）已获知此事。华人侦探长（C.D.I.）施子良（Sih Tse Liang，音译）表示，目前没有关于该纠纷的情报，在特工能够前往浦东之前，无法获取任何情报。已与该公司的布朗先生（Mr. Brown）取得联系，并告知如有必要，特务科将在河这边提供协助。随后，布朗先生转达信息称，麻烦起因于一些长时间与管理层存在劳资纠纷的工人在下午5点（通常的下班时间）拒绝离开工厂，并采取威胁态度。已通知英国驻华领事馆，英国海军小分队登陆进入公司大院。晚上7点，工人们在一项协议达成后离开工厂，协议规定他们中的一部分人……
